items.title: The training window - is a proper subset of seasons better than all of them?
items.note: Raised by 01a 2026-09-08, deliberately not acted on there. The cliff classifier scores 0.39318 macro-F1 trained on 2021-2023 against 0.38027 on the full 2018-2023 -- +0.01291, 3.71x its own reseed floor, by deleting 46% of its training rows. Larger than most feature-group deltas the programme has shipped on, and it is a change to what production trains on. The confound 01a could not close: load_features fits the ordinal encoder on the full 2018-2023 frame BEFORE the split, and 01a subset rows of the already-encoded matrix -- so 01a's arms are internally clean, but a real window change would refit the encoder and drop HYPERSOFT/SUPERSOFT/ULTRASOFT (2018-only, absent from every 2024 eval row), renumbering the rest. So +0.01291 is NOT what a production window change returns. Arms in work/05-model-family.md: encoder refit inside each fit, multi-seed, more than one eval season, and a compound-level-only arm to separate the encoding effect from the regime effect. Check against 08d first -- if the mechanism is compound identity, the real C1-C5 mapping may recover the dropped rows' value rather than confirm they should be dropped. STALE BASELINE 2026-09-09: the +0.01291 above and its 0.38027 full-window comparator were both measured on the CONTAMINATED substrate, before 08e/08f. The full-window cliff headline is now 0.3704769, so every number in this note needs re-measuring before the item is run. 08f-2 also gives the item a second, concrete mechanism it did not have: 2018's circuit_constructor_interaction_s is now identically 0 across all 197 of its panel rows, so an entire training season has lost that feature's variation - which is an argument for excluding 2018 that is independent of the compound-encoding confound, and one 08d cannot recover the way it might recover the compound-identity mechanism.

closed.reason: CLOSED as a completed measurement with a negative answer, not as a failure. Every clause of the definition of done was delivered: a window recommendation per family, each with its delta against that family's own reseed floor, measured with the encoder REFIT INSIDE each fit (the confound 01a could not close), across FIVE season-fold eval seasons rather than 2024 alone, plus a stated verdict on mechanism. 900 fits / 59 min; arms pre-registered in scripts/arms_05d_training_window.py's docstring before running (gate 6); per-seed headlines in ml/artefacts/05d_training_window_arms.json. Gate 1 PASSED on all four unbarred families (full-window cell reproduced the published headline bit-identically). THE ANSWER IS FULL WINDOW FOR EVERY FAMILY. p10: 0 wins in 15 subset-rule cells, monotone. p50: 1 of 15, at 0.68x its reseed floor. p90: 3 of 15, mean negative at every rung. stint_life under 10e's S1x (the set D4 ruled to ship): 0 of 15, monotone. cliff is the only near-miss at k=4 (most recent 4 seasons), winning both eval seasons where it is a proper subset, aggregate +0.00593 = 1.06x its reseed floor -- consistent in sign but one floor, which is not shipping-grade by this programme's convention. 01a's CELL REPLICATES BUT 01a's RULE DOES NOT. The exact cell 01a reported (eval 2024, train 2021-2023) comes back LARGER with the encoder refit inside and 5 seeds: +0.01484 = 2.57x floor, t-CI [+0.0114,+0.0183], p=0.0003, against 01a's +0.01291 = 3.71x. So it is not an encoding artefact. But the same k=3 rule is significantly WORSE on eval 2023 (-0.00307, p=0.013) and negative on 2022 -- the exact limitation 01a flagged ('could be partly 2024-specific') and it does not survive the test. MECHANISM VERDICT: neither regime nor encoding as 01a framed them. Encoding RULED OUT -- arm B (2018's rows and regime kept, its three unique compound levels collapsed to one code) moves cliff/2024 by -0.00004 = -0.03x floor, while the arm C renumbering null moves it MORE (+0.00028). 2018 RULED OUT as the season that hurts -- dropping 2018 alone gives cliff/2024 only +0.00240 (0.42x, p=0.106, CI straddles zero) and is strongly HARMFUL on eval 2020/2021/2022 (-8.35x/-3.95x/-1.02x). What is actually present is family-specific window saturation: cliff and p90 stop gaining past ~4 seasons; p10, p50 and S1x stint-life never saturate. 01a's STRONGEST RECENCY FINDING WAS A HYPERPARAMETER ARTEFACT: 01a had stint life most recency-driven of the five (14-57x floor at matched n). Under the shipped pre-10e params the ladder is incoherent (best k = 1,3,2,1,4 across eval seasons); under S1x the full window wins all five eval seasons monotonically. The window effect was the mis-tuned booster 10d diagnosed and 10e fixed. TWO MECHANISMS THIS ITEM WAS SENT TO CHECK, BOTH VOID. (1) 08d is not on this path and could not be: stg_tyre_allocations covers 2019-2024 (384 rows); the C1-C5 scale did not exist in 2018, so the real Pirelli mapping structurally cannot recover 2018's compound identity, and arm B shows compound identity is not the mechanism anyway. The spec's '08d before a production window change' ordering is moot. (2) This item's own note argued from 08f-2 that 2018 lost circuit_constructor_interaction_s's variation -- that column reaches a model only via cliff_candidate_flag, which 08j PRUNED. On the live 32-feature contract every feature has non-zero sd in 2018 and none has an anomalous 2018 null rate. The note predates the prune. DO NOT REOPEN on a fresh single-eval-season recency result -- that is the shape this item falsified. Reopening requires a multi-eval-season subset gain clearing its family's reseed floor. Full result: work/05-model-family.md '05d - RESULT'.
closed.gate_pass: Gate 1 PASSED (full-window refit bit-identical to the published headline on p10/p50/p90/cliff); gate 6 honoured (arms pre-registered before running); the arm C renumbering null is the gate-4-shaped capacity/information control for the encoding hypothesis. The standing gate was NOT run end-to-end and deliberately so: the verdict is no window change for any family, so there is no candidate change for gates.md to price. DOES NOT GATE FORWARD -- 05d has no dependants in the tree, and its answer removes a pending question rather than unblocking work. It does feed one correction backwards into 01a's record (01a's 2018/compound-identity mechanism section is not supported, and its stint-life recency result is superseded by 10e's retune) and it retires the 08d-before-window-change ordering concern.

items.title: Mondrian-conformal recalibration of the degradation band, keyed on circuit
items.note: Verified 2026-09-07 (IN-SAMPLE - production v11 trains on every season, holdout 2025 unpopulated, and load_scoring_frame scores every lap): pooled coverage 80.38% against nominal 80 with symmetric tails, and by lap-in-stint band 79.9-81.2% (1.3 pts) - but by circuit 72.4-85.6% across 36 circuits with n>=300 (13.2 pts). The band is right on the axes the model reasons about and wrong on circuit identity. Split-conformal over the CQR score with a per-circuit taxonomy; touches no model, needs no refit, cannot regress the headline. Report coverage AND width, before and after, OUT OF SAMPLE - the in-sample figures are the hypothesis, not the baseline. 36 groups were scanned and the two worst reported, so declare the e-value construction (09b). MEASURED 2026-09-16. R4's table VERIFIED on re-scoring (pooled 80.49% vs its 80.38%, per-circuit spread 13.4 pts vs 13.2 over 36 circuits) -- but the spread is mostly RACE-LEVEL NOISE, not circuit identity. ceiling.py::variance_components on per-race coverage grouped by circuit gives circuit ICC 0.024 in-sample against a naive 0.313, i.e. the estimator a per-circuit coverage table structurally IS overstates the circuit component 13x; sd(circuit effect) 0.74 pts against sd(race noise) 4.65 pts. R4 screened at n>=300 LAPS and laps within a race are not independent -- the effective unit is the race, ~4.1 per circuit. R4's own one-directional claim (in-sample spread is a lower bound) is separately CONFIRMED: out of sample spread 28.9 pts, circuit ICC 0.22-0.29. So a circuit effect exists and is unestimable at this data volume. THE FIX IS STRICTLY DOMINATED: shadow fit 2018-2020 / calib 2021-22 / test 2023-24, Mondrian raises per-circuit RMSE about nominal from 6.63 to 8.98 pts and spread from 28.9 to 37.8 pts while costing 13% more band width (7.507s -> 8.493s); reproduces over 200 race-randomised splits (29.6 +/- 8.5 -> 40.4 +/- 12.7), so it is overfitting and not drift. Per-circuit offsets run -0.263s to +6.605s against a pooled +0.225s; Qatar -- a PRE-REGISTERED circuit -- inflates to a 19.37s band covering 99.87%, exactly the failure the acceptance criterion named. Shrinkage (BLUP weight 0.72) closes most of the penalty but converges to doing nothing from above and never beats it, and is not conformal (not an order statistic, no guarantee). Data volume needed: 10-14 races per circuit for SE = half the effect; ~4 available, short by 2-3x. PRE-REGISTERED E-VALUES ALL NULL: both named circuits reverse sign (Mexico 72.4% in-sample -> 85.88% out, E=0.728; Qatar 72.7% -> 81.81%, E=0.949; pooled E=0.690), and the 36-circuit shuffle-rank scan returns E=1.04. Exchangeability cost quantified: pooled conformal delivers 80.02% +/- 2.03% under a race-randomised split and overshoots to 83.72% temporally, a 3.7-point gap. Per edge, 01b was right that the two are in different states: p10 runs hot in both halves (11.9% then 11.0%) while p90 flipped from under-covering on calib (10.99%) to conservative on test (7.87%), so the +0.173s upper-edge correction was applied in the WRONG DIRECTION. RECOMMENDATION: ship no per-circuit offset. offsets.csv is delivered with the per-circuit rows marked not-recommended; the pooled row is the only one keeping its guarantee and production's marginal coverage is already 80.49%, so it is not needed either. Reopen at 10-14 seasons of per-circuit history, or test a coarser taxonomy (circuit archetype) that pools races without pooling away the effect -- untested here. INCIDENTAL: data/marts/mart_degradation_predictions.parquet is STALE (written 2026-09-05, mart rebuilt since) -- reading its stored predictions against the current target gives 78.77% not 80.49%; anything downstream reading that parquet is reading stale predictions. Raw quantile-crossing rate measured at 0.093% (R4 recorded it as structurally unmeasurable from the parquet). No production artefact written; nothing in ml/models/ touched.

closed.reason: Definition of done met (work/11-parallel-surfaces.md): implementations/11a/offsets.csv delivered with a written recommendation against applying the per-circuit rows, plus the statement of what the guarantee covers. Mondrian is strictly dominated out of sample (per-circuit RMSE about nominal 6.63 -> 8.98 pts, width +13%), and the pre-registered E-values are null. Nothing ships. Reopen only with 10-14 races per circuit, or with a coarser taxonomy (circuit archetype), which is untested. Measured before 08m's target fix (the leaf doc carries the STALE banner). The ruling compares Mondrian with pooled on the same rows, so it is not assumed to move - but it has not been re-measured.

items.title: Assemble the stochastic DP over pit timing
items.note: int_pit_strategy_cost_curve (386,036), int_pit_strategy_value (7,129), int_pit_loss_circuit, int_sc_hazard_history (whose own header says it exists 'so a Monte Carlo race simulator could draw an interruption on each simulated lap', and which ml_headroom.md records as consumed by NOTHING) plus the five models are the transition costs, stochastic event process and state dynamics of a published DP formulation (Carrasco Heine & Thraves, CEJOR 2022, incl. the yellow-flag stochastic extension). Assembly, not research. It also changes what the models are SCORED on: expected race time of the induced policy, and a model-vs-oracle policy gap in SECONDS alongside ceiling.py's statistical denominator. SPEC note (R6 Part 3) verified against the warehouse and THREE OF ITS FOUR TABLE CLAIMS ARE STALE: int_pit_strategy_cost_curve holds 414,289 rows not 386,036 (160,540 / 4,257 stints at 'window' scope, 253,749 / 7,089 at 'race'); int_sc_hazard_history holds 149 rows not 36 and is keyed on (circuit_slug, SEASON) since 02d's point-in-time rebuild, with every 2018 row NULL on every rate; and it is NOT unconsumed -- int_pit_strategy_cost_curve.sql reads it as pit_discount_factor, so ml_headroom.md finding #6 and R6's table are both out of date. int_pit_strategy_value (7,129) and int_pit_loss_circuit (36, shrunk loss 19.30-29.61 s) are as described. TWO OF THE FOUR DECLARED STATE DIMENSIONS DO NOT EXIST: next_compound is fixed to the realised choice (max 1 distinct value per stint x scope over all 414,289 rows) so 'compound on stop' is not enumerable, and track position has no transition kernel -- position is recorded per lap but nothing maps 'stop at lap L' to 'position after the stop'. THE COST CURVE READS NO ML PREDICTION AT ALL: its running cost is dim_compounds_season, a lift of the 438-row compound_cliff_params SEED. And int_lap_residual_decomposed subtracts that same seeded curve before forming driver_skill_residual_s, so next_5_lap_cumulative_jump_s is THE SEED'S RESIDUAL, not tyre degradation -- mean -2.163 s per 5 laps over 82,470 rows, i.e. the seed over-charges by ~0.14 s/lap and the degradation trio spends most of its signal undoing it. MEASURED 2026-09-16. DP built as specified (backward induction over lap x tyre age x caution, the Carrasco Heine & Thraves yellow-flag extension), four arms differing only in the unmodelled-degradation path: seed (= the incumbent), model (v11, IN-SAMPLE), shadow (11a's 2018-2020 fit, OUT OF SAMPLE), oracle. Instrument check PASSES 100%: the seed arm reproduces int_pit_strategy_value.optimal_pit_lap_in_stint for 4,257/4,257 stints and 2,649/2,649 dev + 1,391/1,391 test inside the pipeline. ACCEPTANCE 1, reproduction of the realised call at +/-2 valid laps, race-clustered bootstrap n=2000, test half 2023-24 (1,391 stints / 46 races / 24 circuits): production argmin as shipped 33.86% [29.0-38.6], seed DP 38.46% [33.5-43.3], model DP 53.70% [47.3-60.0], SHADOW DP (out of sample) 52.98% [47.0-58.7], oracle DP 32.64% [28.5-36.6]; exact agreement 6.90% -> 21.28%. On the known-good subset (green stint ending + points finish, 607 stints / 45 races) seed 41.35% [35.0-48.0] vs shadow 54.04% [46.4-61.7]. ACCEPTANCE 2, the model-vs-oracle policy gap IN SECONDS: +1.90 s/stint [-0.35, +4.20] -- THE WRONG SIGN, interval covering zero, so it is reported as UNIDENTIFIED per the pre-registration's declared rule. The oracle's apparent 0.10 s regret on the raw surface is entirely winner's curse; a half-sample (odd/even lap) split removes it and the oracle becomes WORSE than the model. What the ML forecast does buy over the seed-only incumbent is +3.59 s/stint [1.64-5.66] out of sample (+3.29 [1.44-5.09] in-sample), but EVERY DP ARM LOSES TO THE HUMANS BY 4.10 s/stint [-5.76, -2.58]. THE STOCHASTIC ARM DOES NOT PAY FOR ITSELF: cautions available in 31.7% of stints at hazard 0.0243/lap, the term moves 37-50% of calls 0.59-1.09 laps later, and switching it OFF is worth +1.01 s [0.45-1.72] on the seed arm and is neutral on the model arms. EXTRAPOLATION POLICY DOMINATES: 'flat' -> 'persist' inflates every regret 4-7x (seed 12.91 -> 75.72 s, shadow 9.32 -> 43.85, human 5.22 -> 69.19) and collapses reproduction 52.98% -> 20.27%. PRE-REGISTERED E-VALUES all far above their declared ceiling of ~8: E1 = 1,996 (38/46 races), E3 = 1,010 (37/46), E2 = 1,000 at the cap (0 of 999 permutations reached 53.70%) -- but none of them tests the acceptance criterion's own quantity, which has no reference point. VERDICT: DO NOT adopt the seconds gap as a headline. Adopt instead, as a SECONDARY diagnostic, the +/-2-lap reproduction rate on the known-good subset with a race-clustered interval: bounded, oracle-free, strategist-readable, and it moves 33.9% -> 53.0% out of sample. INCIDENTAL: fct_lap_residuals carries is_safety_car_lap / is_vsc_lap / is_red_flag_lap and ALL THREE ARE FALSE ON ALL 137,447 ROWS (the mart is pre-filtered to green laps) -- int_stint_geometry is the table with the real flags (8,927 SC / 2,980 VSC / 426 red-flag of 162,729); a first pass read them from the wrong table and got a caution path that silently never fired. mart_degradation_predictions.parquet is CURRENT (v11, 137,447 rows, predicted_at 2026-09-16), contrary to 11a's incidental finding. No production artefact written, no refit, no ONNX re-export, warehouse read-only throughout.

closed.reason: Definition of done met: the DP is assembled and runnable (implementations/11b/s2_dp.py), and the verdict on the induced-policy metric is written - negative on the seconds gap (wrong sign, interval covers zero, unidentified), positive on the +/-2-lap reproduction rate (33.9% -> 53.0% out of sample) as a secondary diagnostic. Nothing shipped. 11b scored v11 predictions, i.e. the pre-08m target and cost curve, so every seconds figure - including D9's +3.59 s/stint - is stale per 08m's own note. D9 stays open and blocks nothing.

items.title: The caution data is all in the warehouse and none of it reaches the app - surface SC/VSC as a live-race fan surface
items.note:
RAISED 2026-09-20 by the fan-value reprioritisation, against the success definition the user stated that day: winning is giving F1 fans stats they can use to settle arguments and something to track live during a race. This is the largest verified gap between what the warehouse holds and what the app can show, and every claim below was traced to source this session rather than taken from a summary.

THE DATA EXISTS. stg_track_status decodes FastF1's raw_track_status into named events (4=safety_car, 5=red_flag, 6=vsc, 7=vsc_ending; stg_track_status.sql:38-46) at one row per status change. stg_laps.sql:123-126 decodes the same digit string to per-lap booleans is_safety_car_lap / is_vsc_lap / is_red_flag_lap, and int_stint_geometry.sql:74-76 carries all three at lap grain. int_sc_hazard_history is a per-(circuit_slug, season) SC/VSC hazard PER RACING LAP, season-lagged since 02d's 2026-09-11 rebuild, and its own header records 148 of 148 races in scope, 100% of every season 2018-2024.

THE APP CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT. A grep over app/src returns ZERO references to int_sc_hazard_history, stg_track_status or int_stint_geometry, and scripts/export_app_data.py's export list names none of the three - so no parquet carrying a caution flag or a hazard rate ever reaches the browser. 10c said the same thing from the modelling side and it is still true: 'it cannot tell the user which cause is coming - the app has no SC term, and int_sc_hazard_history, which is exactly that term, feeds nothing' (work/10-competing-risks.md:937-938).

AND A LIVE PAGE TELLS USERS THE OPPOSITE. app/src/routes/race-craft/race-control.tsx ships with 'This feature requires the FIA race control message feed safety car deployments, VSC periods, red flags, and the lap on which each occurred. That event log is not yet ingested into the pipeline.' That sentence is FALSE today: raw_track_status is ingested, staged and consumed. Whatever this item decides to build, that page's stated reason must stop being wrong - the same class of defect as 00d one level up, a wrong explanation rather than a wrong number.

WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A WIRING JOB, which is also why the model is opus-5. (1) The per-circuit hazard is the number a fan wants ('how likely is a safety car here') and it is the number 11a's measurement says is hardest to defend: at roughly 4.1 races per circuit in this warehouse, ceiling.py::variance_components put the circuit ICC of per-race coverage at 0.024 in sample against a naive 0.313, and 11a's ruling was that a per-circuit effect exists and is unestimable at this data volume. int_sc_hazard_history anticipates exactly this and carries empirical-Bayes-shrunk variants beside the raw rates. This item must RULE which column the app shows and how the uncertainty is expressed, in writing, before anything is exported; shipping a raw per-circuit rate as a bare percentage is the failure 11a exists to prevent. (2) Every 2018 row is NULL on every rate by construction - season-lagged, no prior season - and the model's header is explicit that 'unknowable' and 'measured, no events' are different statements, which is what prior_races_n / prior_racing_laps are for. A COALESCE to zero on the display side erases precisely that distinction. Declare it; do not fill it. (3) Two shipped app queries already filter on caution flags that never fire: app/src/features/race-lost/queries.ts:57-58 and app/src/features/lap-waterfall/queries.ts:59 and :90 apply NOT is_safety_car_lap / NOT is_vsc_lap to fct_lap_residuals, and 11b's incidental verification measured all three flags FALSE on all 137,447 rows of that mart because it is already filtered to green racing laps (work/11-parallel-surfaces.md:754-758). The rows on screen are genuinely green so no displayed number is wrong, but the filter is a no-op and the surrounding methodology text implies it is doing work. Fix it in the same pass, against int_stint_geometry, which is the table with the real flags.

SCOPE GUARD. Touches NO model, NO FEATURE_COLUMNS entry and NO ML artefact - group 11's charter. It does not run 02d's ablation and does not pre-empt it: whether the hazard helps stint_life_regressor is 02d's question and is independent of whether the hazard can be displayed. It does not build the FIA incident/penalty log that app/src/routes/race-craft/stewarding.tsx asks for, which genuinely is not ingested. And it does NOT revive 11b's DP as a 'what would an optimal strategist do' overlay - 11b's own verdict reason 6 is that every DP arm loses to the human strategists by 4.10 s/stint, so shipping it as advice would ship a claim this tree has already refuted.

HOME: group 11, whose header reads 'items that touch no model and block nothing ... convert work that already exists into something a user can read.' That is this item exactly. Leaf doc: work/11-parallel-surfaces.md, 11c. ORDER_HINT 3: the data is built, verified and leak-free, and the only reason it is not on screen is that nobody exported it.

SHARED COLUMN CHOICE WITH 02d, recorded 2026-09-20 by the clubbing pass, and deliberately NOT a merge. int_sc_hazard_history publishes six rate columns - sc_hazard_per_lap, vsc_hazard_per_lap and any_hazard_per_lap at :202-206, and the empirical-Bayes shrunk variant of each at :223-239 - beside prior_races_n and prior_racing_laps. 11c must rule which of those six a fan is shown; 02d must pick which of the same six the ablation feeds to stint_life_regressor. The two rulings answer to DIFFERENT criteria - what can honestly be told to a fan at roughly 4.1 races per circuit, against what earns its place through the gate - and a column can clear one and fail the other, so they are not one ruling and this pass did not fold them together. They are, though, one lookup: 11c runs first (order_hint 3 against 02d's 6), so it should write its column choice and its shrinkage reasoning somewhere 02d will read it, rather than leaving 02d to re-derive the argument from 11a's ICC independently.

LANDED 2026-09-20. RULING FIRST, then wired; full text in work/11-parallel-surfaces.md, '11c - RULING'. THE RULING: the app shows the observed caution timeline as the headline (a record, not an estimate), ONE POOLED caution frequency beside it with a Wilson interval and its race count, and NO per-circuit probability anywhere. WHY: this item re-ran 11a's instrument (ceiling.py::variance_components) on the quantity it proposed to display rather than inheriting 11a's number - per-race caution rate grouped by circuit, 149 races over 36 circuits, 4.14 races/circuit, the same volume 11a had. Circuit ICC comes back 0.000 for BOTH 'P(race has a safety car)' (naive 0.306) and 'P(race has any caution)' (naive 0.285), and 0.005 for the caution lap share (naive 0.403): the between-circuit mean square falls BELOW the within-circuit one, so the ANOVA estimator clamps the circuit variance component to zero. That is STRONGER than 11a's finding - 11a found a circuit effect too small to estimate (ICC 0.024, sd 0.74 pts vs 4.65 pts race noise); this finds none to estimate. The scan confirms it: per-circuit SE at 4.14 races is 22.3 pts, 36 circuits of pure noise spread an expected 94.7 pts best-to-worst, and the OBSERVED spread is 100.0 pts - eight circuits read exactly 100% (Azerbaijan 6/6, Mexico City 4/4, Saudi 4/4, Sao Paulo 4/4, Qatar 3/3...) and one reads 0%. 'Baku: 100% chance of a safety car' is six coin flips. COLUMN CHOICE (the lookup 02d was told to read): the *_shrunk columns only; the raw per-circuit rates are never read into the app. Raw any_hazard_per_lap spans 0.00000-0.10000 over the 128 rows with a prior season; the shrunk variant spans 0.01850-0.03258, a 1.8x range. The reason the shrunk column is safe is also the reason it is nearly uninformative, and the page says so: with the 600-lap EB pseudo-count the own-data weight L/(L+600) averages 0.178 and never exceeds 0.413, so ~82% of every shrunk value is the all-circuits pooled rate wearing a circuit's name. 02d should weigh that before feeding any of the six columns to stint_life_regressor - its criterion is the gate, not fan-honesty, so it may still rule differently, but it should not re-derive this. POOLED HEADLINE, Wilson 95%, 149 races: any caution 110/149 = 73.8% [66.2-80.2]; safety car 85/149 = 57.0% [49.0-64.7]; VSC 65/149 = 43.6% [35.9-51.6]; red flag 19/149 = 12.8% [8.3-19.1]; 8.97% of all race laps ran under caution. The one real movement is SEASONAL, not spatial - 90.5% (2018) and 90.9% (2022) against 58.3% (2024), a 32-point range against a zero circuit component - and it ships on the page rather than being averaged away. 2018 DECLARED, NOT FILLED: all 21 of its rows are NULL on every rate (season-lagged, no prior season); 36 rows are NULL on the raw rate (2018's 21 plus 15 circuit debuts); only those 21 are NULL on the shrunk rate. The page prints 'not measurable' and draws no bar - no COALESCE, because a measured zero and an unmeasurable one are different claims. 11b's FLAGS CLAIM RE-MEASURED AND IT HOLDS EXACTLY: fct_lap_residuals 137,447 rows, is_safety_car_lap / is_vsc_lap / is_red_flag_lap TRUE on 0 and NULL on 0 - the three predicates dropped exactly zero rows. int_stint_geometry 162,729 rows / 8,927 SC / 2,980 VSC / 426 red, also exact. Both no-op filters REMOVED (race-lost/queries.ts, lap-waterfall/queries.ts x2) with the measurement recorded in a header comment, and the four places whose methodology text implied the query was doing the exclusion were corrected to say it happens upstream in the mart (two methodology.tsx, docs/app/lap-waterfall.mdx, docs/app/race-lost.mdx). No displayed number moved, which was already known. SHIPPED: int_sc_hazard_history added to export_app_data.py's TABLES (149 rows, 8.5 KB) plus a new DERIVED_TABLES mechanism carrying race_caution_timeline - one row per (race, lap) from int_stint_geometry's BOOL_OR'd flags, 8,929 rows / 801 caution laps / 6.2 KB. race-craft/race-control.tsx is a real feature (app/src/features/race-control/, 12 unit tests), shipped in nav with the race-craft pillar restored, docs/app/race-control.mdx and families/race-craft.mdx added, app_docs_audit 31/31 strict PASS. Timeline cross-checked two ways: contiguous SC lap-runs reconstruct 112 windows against stg_track_status's 119 logged onsets with 76/85 races agreeing exactly (merged back-to-back deployments explain the gap), and the caution-flagged race set agrees with stg_race_control's SafetyCar messages on 146/149. INCIDENTAL, AND IT CORRECTS THIS ITEM'S OWN SCOPE GUARD: the FIA race-control MESSAGE feed IS INGESTED. transform/models/staging/stg_race_control.sql stages data/bronze/race_control/ - 12,814 messages over all 149 races 2018-2024, with message_category (383 SafetyCar, 457 Drs, 246 CarEvent), flag (26 RED, 4,909 BLUE), message_text, driver_id, and a lap_number on every safety-car message. Its own header says it is consumed by nothing and grep confirms no model or export reads it. So race-control.tsx's old sentence was wrong twice over, and stewarding.tsx and /roadmap carried the same error; all three were corrected to the true statement, which is that the PENALTY/OUTCOME STRUCTURE is missing (decisions live as free text in message_text), not the feed. The penalty log was NOT built - out of scope. CONTRACT UNMOVED: python3 -m ml.src.features --check CLEAN at 32 features with fingerprint 7852405cfa4abd474db3a658beb883b8e2b72acda475298867b9b2584d55d8f1, byte-identical to the pre-session baseline. No model, no FEATURE_COLUMNS entry, no ML artefact, no dbt model touched; 02d's ablation not run and not pre-empted; 11b's DP not revived. ONE THING FOR A HUMAN: the full `make app-data` run this item needed (to restore the manifest after --table mode, which rewrites it with only the named table - a pre-existing sharp edge in that script) refreshed app/public/data/ml/mart_degradation_predictions/*.parquet for all 7 seasons with GENUINELY DIFFERENT content. The committed export predated the 2026-09-16 19:42 rebuild of data/marts/mart_degradation_predictions.parquet, so the published app data was stale against the warehouse. That refresh belongs to 08n/10e, not to this item; it is in the working tree for the user to include or drop.

items.title: Real Pirelli C1-C5 compound identity per race (2019-present), hand-sourced from press.pirelli.com
items.note: Opened 2026-09-08, out of a user question about whether SOFT/MEDIUM/HARD naming (relative since 2019) needs the underlying C-number tracked anywhere. It doesn't currently. Not a repair like 08a -- dim_compounds_season's circuit x compound x season grain already avoids pooling different physical rubber under one label, so nothing is broken. This is new information: the absolute C1-C5 scale, which would let compound severity be compared across circuits and cross-check the fitted grip_peak/wear_gradient ordering. stg_tyre_allocations.sql already exists as an empty stub with the right shape, built for exactly this and never filled in. Two LLM-generated attempts at this table were rejected this session as fabricated -- both invented a compound called 'Ice Hard' (not real, no season), one was internally self-contradictory (a compound named as both present and skipped for the same race), and one asserted Monaco/Singapore 2025 raced on C6 when the sourced fact is that C6 was a limited test at Mexico City and Abu Dhabi in 2024, not raced at those two circuits in 2025. This item must be sourced from real press.pirelli.com nomination posts or season-recap articles, cited per season, not regenerated from a model's prior knowledge -- see work/08-foundations-repair.md. BUILT 2026-09-10 ON USER-SUPPLIED DATA, NOT SOURCED. seeds/tyre_allocations.csv holds 128 rows (one per race, wide: race_year, circuit_key, hard_code, medium_code, soft_code, source_url); stg_tyre_allocations unpivots to 384 rows at (race,label) grain; 16 dbt tests pass; ALL 127 mart races in 2019-2024 match, so the join is total. The 128th row is (2021, belgian_grand_prix), the rain-shortened race -- in int_stint_geometry but not the mart. It does the item's job: 2024 SOFT resolves to C3 at Bahrain/Silverstone/Zandvoort/Suzuka/Qatar/Barcelona but C4 at Spa/Shanghai. The data is user-supplied and self-verified, accepted on explicit instruction to unblock downstream work. MEASURED: only 47 of 128 source_url values resolve, 81 return 404 -- a URL in that column is an attribution, not evidence. Three revisions were rejected first: rev 1 repeated the exact C6-at-Monaco/Singapore-2025 fabrication this item already names, with zero citations; rev 2 was 59% unusable (all 2019 cited a search-results page that names no compounds, all 2020 cited a 404, all 2021 cited a PRE-SEASON list that includes four cancelled races, omits Styria/Turkey/Qatar which cite it, and contradicts its own Austria row) and used nine keys absent from the warehouse. Rev 3 fixed the keys and moved to per-race previews. 2024 Monza VERIFIED 2026-09-10: user-supplied data has C3/C4/C5 (not the rev 2 C3/C4/C5 -> C2/C3/C4 change in rev 3), Hard White C3 2 sets / Yellow C4 3 sets / Red C5 8 sets per Pirelli's own allocation. DECISION 2026-09-10: accept current table as NON-QUOTABLE convenience for internal use, allowing measurement to proceed without citing these rows as claims (epistemics.md line). Open separate sourcing item for proper archival re-source of 2019-2022 (FIA event documents) when capacity permits. Until proper sourcing, nothing measured against this table may be quoted as a claim. A full dbt build was run 2026-09-10 and completed successfully (720 PASS, 0 ERROR, 723 TOTAL) -- mart anchors at 137,447 rows / 121,193 training-eligible / 98.275% push_residual coverage, matching the 08e/08f baselines exactly. Nothing committed. VERIFIED 2026-09-17: user confirms full correctness of 128-row mapping table across 2019-2024. Landed as is.

items.title: Thermal-proxy stint baseline reaches forward - rebuild as a trailing window
items.note: Opened 2026-09-09 by 08b's new audit. int_lap_thermal_proxy.stint_baseline_agg is MEDIAN(lap_time_s) FILTER (lap_in_stint <= CEIL(stint_length_actual*0.60)) GROUP BY stint_id. Two verified reaches: 55.92% of 137,447 mart rows are scored against laps that had not yet run (mean 4.65, max 45; 100% at lap_in_stint=2 at mean 11.83), and the cutoff is a function of stint_length_actual, which equals fct_stint_features.stint_length_laps exactly (8,333/8,333, r=1.0) -- the stint-life target's numerator. Reaches push_residual, cumulative_push_load_surface, cumulative_push_load_bulk, surface_bulk_ratio. DEGRADATION_TARGET is next_5_lap_cumulative_jump_s so the mean reach sits inside the label's own window, the same thing that decided 02a. Rebuild as a trailing/expanding median over strictly-prior laps with a min-observation floor; share the trailing-median macro with 02g (R5 recommendation 2). Measure materiality first, 02a's template. Also extend assert_no_future_leakage to check push_residual itself, not only the EWMA over it. MATERIALITY MEASURED 2026-09-09 (work/08-foundations-repair.md, '08e materiality'). Probe reproduces production exactly (162,729/162,729 rows, stint_baseline_pace and push_residual bit-for-bit). Defect 2 is exact: baseline_cutoff_lap == GREATEST(CEIL(stint_length_laps*0.60),3) on 121,193/121,193 training-eligible mart rows, corr(cutoff, remaining_stint_life_laps)=+0.5644. Position-matched on lap_in_stint (21 strata, n=85,693) the BLOCK->TRAILING swing clears in ALL THREE families: degradation -0.0350 [-0.0633,-0.0073] p=0.010, cliff P(0-2) -0.0357 [-0.0518,-0.0230] p=0.000, stint-life +0.1055 [+0.0361,+0.1776] p=0.001. Measured here the four floors give clearly different headlines in every family (stint-life 1.9926008/1.9913359/1.9880619/1.9909305). That arm never varied. Its quoted coverage numbers (94.79%, 89.46%) reproduce nothing measurable here. STEP 1 PASSES ON BOTH HALVES. 1a: the floor-2 arm reproduces the published v12 headline EXACTLY (|diff| = 0.00e+00) on all five families. 1b: a floor-parameterised replica of int_lap_thermal_proxy's window logic reproduces the BUILT warehouse BIT-FOR-BIT on push_residual, both cumulative loads and surface_bulk_ratio -- 137,447/137,447 rows each, NULL counts identical (14,017/14,017/14,017/27,287) -- so floors 1/3/5 are that same query with one integer changed rather than a reimplementation. STRUCTURAL FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE ITEM: is_training_eligible is age_in_stint > 3 AND anomaly_class NOT IN ('mistake','conditions') and NEVER references the thermal block, so the floor turns values into NaN and NEVER deletes a row. The leaf doc's central hazard -- 'a headline that improves by deleting the hard rows' -- is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT; eval rows are identical at every floor (13,712/13,712/18,866/19,973). The cross-floor contrast is therefore capacity-neutral by construction (same 32 columns, same rows, same split); step 4 was run anyway because 'not capacity' is not 'not noise'. RESULT -- THE TRADE DOES NOT EXIST. 08e priced floors above 1 as buying degradation signal for coverage. They cost BOTH. Coverage on the training-eligible panel: floor 1 98.20%, floor 2 96.05% (built), floor 3 90.70%, floor 5 80.35%. Cross-floor deltas vs the built floor 2 (positive = improvement, quoted against the LARGER of the two arms' 5-reseed floors, 08g's convention): FLOOR 3 CLEARS AGAINST on p10 -0.0108640 (-2.10x), p90 -0.0121094 (-1.44x), cliff -0.0050280 (-1.11x); FLOOR 5 CLEARS AGAINST on p10 -0.0244327 (-2.29x), p90 -0.0145802 (-1.57x), cliff -0.0070541 (-1.00x, marginal at 1.0019x its own floor). FLOOR 1 CLEARS FOR on p50 +0.0139527 (+1.25x, E=13.46 improvement) and is inside its floor elsewhere (p10 +0.16x, p90 +0.38x, cliff -0.36x, life -0.19x) -- no family moved against by more than its own floor. EVERY missingness-only control (shuffled(F) - shuffled(2), both sides row-shuffled so only NaN density differs) is small, |0.09x| to |0.39x|, so the damage at floors 3 and 5 is DESTROYED INFORMATION, not NaN density. STEP 4: the thermal block carries real information at EVERY floor (+1.41x to +50.86x its own floor, E 18.5-35.9), consistent with 08e's family-T finding -- what the floor changes is HOW MUCH, and more floor means less: indicative information sums 0.2249 (f1) / 0.2142 (f2) / 0.1859 (f3) / 0.1624 (f5). stint_life_regressor is the single exception (information rises monotonically with the floor) and its headline delta still never clears. HEADLINES: all three degradation heads prefer floor 1 (p10 0.4753878, p50 0.9684060, p90 0.5072930 vs floor 2's 0.4764641 / 0.9823587 / 0.5128462); cliff prefers floor 2 and life prefers floor 3, both by less than their own floor. items.title: The seed compound curve that defines the degradation target - quantify its bias, rule on a refit
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-16. Premise corrected: compound_cliff_params is NOT hand-written placeholder values -- git log and dev.duckdb's built table (fit_date/fit_source columns checked directly) confirm it was refit via transform/tasks/coefficients/fit_compound_cliff.py + survival.py on 2026-07-30 and again 2026-09-08/09, before this item was opened and before int_compound_cliff_predicted.sql's 'placeholder values' header comment was last touched (2026-09-07). That fit is a legitimate, non-circular anchor (normalized_pace_s -- dirty-air-corrected driven pace -- whose full dependency chain carries no reference to compound_cliff_params, dim_compounds_season, int_compound_cliff_predicted or int_lap_residual_decomposed; KM survival for onset, wind-controlled OLS for wear gradient, pre/post window difference for severity). QUANTIFY (ACCEPTANCE): the target next_5_lap_cumulative_jump_s decomposes exactly into seed_bias(t) = -(seed's own forward-window change in expected_compound_pace_s) plus rest(t). Over 95,346 non-null rows: target mean -1.8793s (reproduces prior reads exactly), seed_bias mean -3.5853s, rest mean +1.7059s, seed_bias/target fraction 1.9077x, race-clustered 95% CI [1.7638, 2.0825] (147 races, 2000 resamples, intervals.py::cluster_bootstrap). Training-eligible subset (82,470 rows): fraction 1.7552x, CI [1.6378, 1.8984]. The seed subtracts MORE than the whole target and same-signed, so rest (net of the seed's own contribution) is POSITIVE (+1.7s/5 laps) -- opposite sign to the published target. ATTRIBUTION: of the unbounded seed_bias, only 20.7% is the correctly-scaled fitted linear wear_gradient*age term; 18.9% is a hardcoded, never-fit 0.002*age^2 constant; 60.4% is fitted cliff_severity*laps_past_cliff, but compound_cliff_severity is fit (survival.py::estimate_cliff_severity, own docstring) as a LEVEL shift over a ~5-lap post-cliff window (median 0.77s) and consumed in the SQL as a PER-LAP RATE (laps_past_cliff reaches 48 in the data) -- a units/interpretation bug in int_compound_cliff_predicted.sql (and independently reimplemented in int_pit_strategy_cost_curve.sql, the running cost 11b's DP and D9 depend on), not a seed-value problem. ORCHESTRATION CORRECTION 2026-09-16: the run's claim that the cost-curve path is 'unbounded'/'uncapped'/'worse' is WRONG and is corrected in the leaf doc -- int_pit_strategy_cost_curve.sql:189-194 applies the SAME shared LEAST(..., var('compound_wear_max_s_per_lap', 10.0)) to the same three terms, and the '136 s/lap at age 80' line the run quoted as evidence is from the comment explaining why that cap exists. Both age-dependent curves are bounded at 10 s/lap; the ruling stands unchanged (a 10 s/lap cap does not repair a per-lap-vs-level-shift unit error), but the two lineage paths are equivalent duplicates of one bug, not one worse than the other. RULING: decline the seed refit (it can only move the 20.7% linear-term share; the 79% majority lives in the formula, not the seed's numbers) -- keep the seed, bias documented above as a known property of the target. FLAGGED, NOT MADE (dbt model write, barred by this item's constraints): fix int_compound_cliff_predicted.sql and int_pit_strategy_cost_curve.sql to consume severity as a genuine per-lap slope (or cap/decay laps_past_cliff's multiplier) and to fit rather than hardcode the quadratic coefficient; recommended as a new item (candidate 08m), not opened here. EXTRA (worth having): a zero-fit seed-echo predictor (seed_bias(t) + one train-fit constant per quantile, scored via train.py::pinball_loss on evaluate.py's own cv_final_fold split) captures 88.6% / 92.6% / 89.0% of degradation_regressor p10/p50/p90's ENTIRE measured pinball-skill margin over the model_card.yml baseline -- only 7-11% of the trio's published 'beats baseline' margin is anything beyond reconstructing the seed's own known arithmetic. BLAST RADIUS: no refit taken, so no rebuild-and-diff table; group 10 (stint_life_regressor) verified NOT implicated (target sourced from stint_length_laps - lap_in_stint, no dependency on driver_skill_residual_s or the seed); 11a, 11b, and the degradation_regressor-family arms in 08e/08f/08h/08i and 02b/02c/02d/02g directly implicated (the latter group ASSUMED per leaf-doc framing, not individually re-verified this session); cliff_classifier partially/related-but-unquantified, flagged not measured. Full numbers, formulas and the RESULT section: work/08-foundations-repair.md 08l.

items.title: The severity units bug - fix how the SQL consumes the seed, rebuild the target, re-price everything measured against the old one
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-16. The dbt change IS in the warehouse (data/dev.duckdb rebuilt, 20/20 models, 225/225 dbt tests pass) but only gate step 1 of six genuinely ran, so this is MEASURED, not LANDED or GATED. RULING: (A) -- keep the seed, correct the consumption. Argued in writing in the leaf doc BEFORE any SQL was edited. Decisive reason: compound_cliff_severity is itself a published ML feature (schema.py:124, attribution.py:107, model_card.yml:43/:78), so (B) would have silently re-defined a contract column's units without changing its name; and (B)'s post-cliff slope cannot be identified -- the post-onset region is short and censored in the one direction that biases it (drivers pit to escape the cliff), which KM handles for onset and nothing in survival.py handles for a slope. Seed values, dim_compounds_season's contract and survival.py are all UNTOUCHED. THE FIX, defined once in a new macro transform/macros/compound_cliff_wear.sql so the sites cannot drift: excess = GREATEST(severity - 5.5*wear_gradient, 0); plateau = 2.2*excess; term(k) = plateau*LEAST(k,5.5)/5.5. Two corrections: de-double-counting (the curve already charges wear_gradient*age across the same 5.5-lap centroid separation the severity windows straddle, so 48.7% of measured severity -- mean 0.4385s of 0.8996s -- was ordinary wear charged twice), and moment-matching then saturation (the 2.2 gain makes the corrected curve reproduce the fitter's own two-window difference exactly; past onset+5.5 the fitter measured nothing so the curve holds flat). The 0.002*age^2 quadratic is DROPPED everywhere: never fitted, identical across all 438 cells, and already absorbed by the linear term since _fit_wear_slope_with_wind fits pace ~ [1, age, wind] with no quadratic in its design matrix. Median cell: the severity term at laps_past_cliff=48 goes from 40.8s to a 1.023s plateau. SIX SITES, not the four the spec listed (spec block corrected). Fixed: int_compound_cliff_predicted's expected_compound_pace_s AND its expected_degradation_rate_s_per_lap derivative (which carried a THIRD defect 08l never reported -- it added full severity on every lap with NO hinge, charging a fresh lap-1 tyre the whole cliff severity), int_pit_strategy_cost_curve (confirmed a duplicate, not worse -- the orchestration correction to 08l was right), and fct_ghost_car_pace's cliff_interaction_s (site 5, in neither 08l nor the spec). NOT fixed and marked in code: int_constructor_deg_sensitivity:380 severity_used (site 6) -- it uses severity as an s/lap^2 divisor whose correct replacement has median ~0.17 against severity's ~0.85, so the GREATEST(...,0.30) floor on that same line, calibrated to the old scale, would bind on nearly every cell and clamp cliff_onset_shift_laps for the whole field; re-deriving that floor is a measurement with its own acceptance test, not a line edit. survival.py NOT touched (correct under ruling A). ACCEPTANCE 1 (the ratio) FAILED AS WRITTEN and the criterion is ill-posed -- corrected in the spec block. seed_bias/target went 1.9077x [1.7638,2.0825] -> 3.4518x [2.7323,4.5800], AWAY from 1.0, because the ratio's denominator is the target's own mean, which a successful fix drives toward zero; it diverges precisely when the fix works. Both un-normalised quantities moved hard the right way: target mean -1.8793 -> -0.3946s (79% closer to zero), seed_bias -3.5853 -> -1.3620s (62% smaller). What survives from 08l qualitatively: |seed_bias| still exceeds |target| same-signed, so rest still carries the opposite sign (+0.967 vs -0.395) -- the bias is substantially reduced, NOT eliminated. But what REMAINS is now mostly legitimate: post-fix seed_bias is 79.4% the fitted wear_gradient*age term (-1.0819s, matching 08l's independent figure exactly) and 20.6% cliff ramp + temperature -- an INVERSION of 08l's attribution, where only ~21% was the correctly-scaled fitted term. ACCEPTANCE 2 (seed-echo share, scale-free, the load-bearing test) PASSES DECISIVELY: 88.60/92.62/88.98% -> 39.69/49.90/23.54% on p10/p50/p90. THE BIAS WAS REMOVED, NOT RELOCATED. Run at fixed target through the production path only (F.load_features -> E._evaluation_split -> E.baseline_predictions -> E._fit -> E._score), in memory, writing nothing, against BOTH warehouses (the scratchpad rollback copy for 'old' and the rebuilt one for 'new') so both columns come from one instrument rather than comparing against a differently-produced published number. Conservative: the rebuilt-target models used published v11 hyperparameters, not a re-search, so a re-tuned model would push the share lower still. THE TRAP, honoured: model_card.yml's 1.04679 and this session's 0.98236 are NOT compared -- they are losses on different quantities (target mean -1.8793 -> -0.3946s, population 82,470 -> 81,619 rows). No model-improvement claim is made by this item. BLAST RADIUS: cliff_classifier QUANTIFIED, which 08l flagged as ASSUMED and did not measure -- 14,833 of 137,447 labels changed class (10.79%), none_in_stint 69.3%->63.6% and 6_plus 11.1%->15.5%, confirming the over-charged curve was erasing cliff crossings into the majority class. is_training_eligible net -1,371 (82,470 -> 81,619), making model_card.yml's n_training_rows stale. 08e/08f/08h/08i, 02 and 11a marked STALE with banners in their own leaf docs (deltas remain valid relative to each other; rulings stand). 11b/D9's +3.59 s/stint rides on the changed cost curve and is stale. Group 10 not affected. PRODUCTION ARTEFACTS STALE AND UNTOUCHED (barred): ml/models/*, model_card.yml and mart_degradation_predictions.parquet are all now inconsistent with the warehouse; retrain was in-memory only. Also found: ml/tests/test_features.py::test_aggregation_survey_still_names_the_outstanding_instance fails (198 pass, 1 fail) -- PRE-EXISTING and not caused here (this session touched neither int_sc_hazard_history.sql nor ml/tests/). 02d rebuilt that model as season-lagged on 2026-09-11; transform/target/ is gitignored and the on-disk manifest predated it, so a stale manifest had been masking a stale test until this session's dbt run regenerated it. Left unfixed deliberately -- it belongs to 02d. Rollback: dev.duckdb was 1.4 GB (under 5 GB) so it was copied to the scratchpad before the first dbt run. Nothing committed.

items.title: Rebuild the shipped artefacts against the fixed target
items.note: LANDED 2026-09-16. Shipped as v12, NOT as a v11 overwrite. THE VERSION RULING, argued in the leaf doc BEFORE the first booster was trained: (1) the codebase already states this policy in train.py::_guard_target_change's own docstring -- refitting across a target change would replace 'the rollback point for everything after them ... with models of a DIFFERENT QUANTITY under the same name, the same artefact path and an unchanged manifest', and its stated remedy is 'Use a new --version for the new target'; (2) direct precedent -- MODEL_VERSION_DEFAULT's own v10 note records that v10 was cut precisely BECAUSE a target/label change had been living under a stale v6 label; (3) v11's numbers are cited all over this tree (model_card.yml, D3, 08m's fresh STALE banners, the docs MDX), and overwriting v11 would make those citations unfalsifiable rather than merely stale; (4) v11 is the rollback floor and the only artefact set fitted to the pre-08m target -- overwriting destroys the only thing left to diff against; (5) D2 (production still on v6) becomes tractable as v6 -> v12 with v11 intact between them. The counter-argument was weighed in writing: 08k rebuilt v11 IN PLACE eleven days ago, but 08j changed the FEATURE CONTRACT (33->32) and a refit on a different feature set still predicts the same quantity, whereas 08m changed the TARGET -- and _guard_target_change guards the target and not the feature set, which is the project's own line and puts 08k on the legitimate side of it. v12 = v11's 32-feature contract + v11's hyperparameters, refitted against the post-08m warehouse; nothing else moved, so v11 -> v12 is attributable to 08m alone. BEATS-BASELINE ON THE REBUILT TARGET, each model vs its OWN baseline in the same run (eval_season 2024, cv_final_fold): p10 0.47646 vs 0.73368; p50 0.98236 vs 1.26289; p90 0.51285 vs 0.64268; cliff_classifier macro-F1 0.35247 vs 0.20667; stint_life AFT NLL 1.99134 vs 2.18868. ALL FIVE BEAT BASELINE, all_claims_significant=true, claims_inside_noise=[]. NO TARGET REGRESSED against its own baseline, so the spec's 'that is a finding, do not repair it' branch never fired and nothing was tuned or reweighted. INSTRUMENT CHECK: the trio's production numbers reproduce 08m's in-memory probe to FIVE DECIMALS on all six cells, so 08m's seed-echo shares (39.69/49.90/23.54%, down from 88.6/92.6/89.0%) carry to the shipped v12 artefacts without re-measurement. THE TRAP, honoured: v11's p50 1.04679 and v12's 0.98236 are NOT compared -- different quantity (target mean -1.8793 -> -0.3946 s), different rows (82,470 -> 81,619 train, 13,896 -> 13,712 eval). The BASELINE itself fell 2.17766 -> 1.26289, a 42% drop on a predictor that learns nothing, which is the cleanest demonstration that the loss scale moved and not the skill. NO IMPROVEMENT-OVER-v11 CLAIM IS MADE ANYWHERE. The model card now carries that statement as its FIRST limitation (added to ml/src/card.py so it survives regeneration), and it propagated to ml/models/model_card.json, app/public/models/model_card.json and docs/reference/ml/degradation-model.mdx. SPEC CORRECTED IN TWO PLACES, both about stint_life_regressor, which the spec called 'not implicated': it IS implicated on two counts and its v11 artefacts were NOT still valid. (i) Two of its 32 INPUTS -- expected_compound_pace_s and expected_degradation_rate_s_per_lap, both in FEATURE_GROUPS['cliff_prior'] -- were rewritten by 08m. (ii) Its ROW SET moved 121,193 -> 119,822, traced end to end: features.py:124 filters every target by is_training_eligible; fct_cliff_prediction_features.sql:749-754 defines that from anomaly_class; int_lap_anomaly_flags.sql:245 computes anomaly_class from driver_skill_residual_s, which is what 08m changed. This also reconciles 08m's note, which reports 'net -1,371' beside '82,470 -> 81,619' (-851): both are correct and they are DIFFERENT POPULATIONS -- -1,371 is the is_training_eligible flag count (stint_life's population), -851 is the trio's, which additionally needs a non-null target. Its TARGET values are genuinely unchanged (verified: features.py:165 synthesises remaining_stint_life_laps as clip(stint_length_laps - lap_in_stint, 0, None)), so it is THE ONE TARGET where a v11/v12 before/after statement is admissible in kind: margin over baseline 0.19905 -> 0.19735 on a 1.5% smaller eval set, i.e. materially unchanged -- 08m's repair neither helped nor hurt it, which is the expected result for a model whose target never moved. FINDING, no item opened (not this session's call): _guard_target_change CANNOT FIRE for a definition change. It compares target_column STRINGS, and 08m changed the column's meaning while leaving its name alone, so it returns at its 'existing == spec.source_column' early-out; the fingerprint check that would have caught it (the fingerprint DID move, 0e8700ec -> 7852405c) is unreachable, gated behind 'target_column is None'. A v11 retrain-in-place would have been SILENT: no error, no warning, right input width, passing parity, plausible manifest. Only the hand-made version ruling stood in the way. items.title: Fix the stint-life calibration defect - the model over-predicts tyre life
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-10. THE DEFECT AS SPECIFIED DOES NOT EXIST AS DESCRIBED: the 1.232 slope was an IN-SAMPLE number, and out of sample the slope is 0.666 - on the other side of 1.0. GATE 1 CAUGHT IT, which is what gate 1 is for. evaluate_10c.py loaded the shipped stint_life_regressor_v11.bst and scored it on cv_final_fold's eval rows, but train.py refits the shipped booster on EVERY training season and training_seasons is 2018-2024, while the eval fold IS 2024 - so every 10c number measured memorisation. Reproduced to six decimals before anything was built on the repair: an all-seasons refit under the 10b label returns green-pit Brier 0.141216 / AUC 0.844167 / slope 1.231641 against 10c's published 0.1412159702194419 / 0.8441673881692147 / 1.2316409494909957, with the 5-bin table matching row for row. OPTIMISM on identical eval rows: AUC 0.8344 in-sample vs 0.6914 honest (+0.1429), Brier 0.1407 vs 0.2059 (-0.0652), slope 1.2346 vs 0.6664 (+0.5682). The slope does not merely shrink across that gap, it CROSSES 1.0, so 10c reported the miscalibration with the WRONG SIGN and every downstream statement inherits that. AUC 0.844 is NOT the incumbent; 0.691 is. Two further facts fell out: the .bst had been rewritten by a standard-variant retrain (training log stint_life_regressor_v11_20260910T092333.json) AFTER 10c ran, so 10c's description of the artefact as 'the 10b-trained model' was already false when it was read; and tune.py calls load_features with the default censoring_variant='standard' over 2018-2024, so max_depth 8 and scale 0.8 were selected against the OTHER label construction, on the mixture NLL 10c said not to use as a headline, with 2024 in the validation set. HONEST BASELINE (refit 2018-2023, scored 2024, 10b labels, tuned v11 params): green-pit slope 0.666, 95% [0.463, 0.906] on a 200-draw race-level cluster bootstrap over 24 eval races, 99.5% of draws below 1.0; AUC 0.691; Brier 0.206. Gate-3 reseed floor with XGBoost's seed genuinely varied (10b's zero-variance reseed table came from not varying it): slope sd 0.006208, floor 2*sqrt(2)*sd = 0.017559; AUC sd 0.001256, floor 0.003554. 10c's SELECTION CHECK SURVIVES, only its sign changed: out of sample zero-SC races 0.6555 (n=7,588, 16 races) vs SC races 0.7823 (n=1,682, 8 races) vs all races 0.6664 - both strata sit well below 1.0, so selection does not explain the defect. ARMS, all selected on the training side only (expanding season folds inside 2018-2023; nothing selected on the 2024 rows). A1 - THE AFT SCALE IS NOT THE LEVER, the clearest negative of the four: across 0.30-1.40, a 4.6x range, the inner-fold green-pit slope moves only 0.537->0.622 and never reaches 0.63; on 2024 the best scale buys +0.022 slope for -0.007 AUC (2.0x the AUC floor), paying more in discrimination than it returns. The inner-CV NLL optimum under the 10b label is 0.90 not the shipped 0.80, so the scale IS mis-set - it just does not matter here. A2 - THE DISTRIBUTION IS NOT THE LEVER EITHER and R2's skew statistic was measured on the wrong quantity: screened on XGBoost's own aft-nloglik over the inner folds, normal 1.8364 beats extreme 1.8650 and logistic 1.8876, so the arm selects the incumbent and nothing needs plumbing through laps_from_margin, the ONNX export and app/src/ml/survival.ts (extreme would have needed all three, its standardised median being log(log 2) = -0.3665, not 0). The reason the direction fails: skewness -0.829 and excess kurtosis 5.218 are properties of the TARGET IN LAPS, but AFT assumes the LOG-SCALE RESIDUAL is normal, and that residual is skew -0.443 / excess kurtosis -0.063 - already near-normal on the scale the model actually uses. A3 - the label construction is worth revisiting, but not for the slope: standard and 10b are indistinguishable on slope (0.700 vs 0.666, 1.9x floor, paired interval straddling zero), but standard is BETTER on green-pit Brier out of sample, 0.190 vs 0.206, better on the level bias (mean log residual -0.285 vs -0.434) and costs no AUC. 10b's label change makes green-pit WORSE out of sample on the metric 10c chose as its headline - a finding about 10b, recorded for whoever rules on it. A4 - CAPACITY IS THE LEVER, and the relationship is monotone. Inner-fold slope 0.794 / 0.708 / 0.680 / 0.669 / 0.656 / 0.622 at max_depth 2/3/4/5/6/8, while inner-fold NLL ALSO improves (1.8171 / 1.8090 / 1.8078 / 1.8130 / 1.8188 / 1.8364) - the shipped max_depth 8 is worse on the training folds' own headline metric, which is what you expect from hyperparameters selected under a different label construction. On 2024: depth 3 slope 0.879 (AUC 0.687, 1.2x AUC floor), depth 2 slope 1.074 (AUC 0.683, 2.5x), against A0 0.666 (AUC 0.691). Depth 2 and the standard-label cross are UNDECLARED extensions added after seeing the monotone trend, logged as such; the declared A4 winner is depth 3. Mechanism visible in the fit: the sd of the margin over green-pit eval rows falls 0.642 -> 0.509 -> 0.418 as depth goes 8 -> 3 -> 2. The incumbent's risk score was OVER-DISPERSED relative to its real skill, which is exactly what a slope below 1.0 means. THE TRADE-OFF THAT WAS NOT ANTICIPATED, and the reason this does not close as a win: reducing capacity fixes the DISPERSION of the risk score and leaves the LEVEL where it was. The calibration intercept only moves +0.271 -> +0.192 -> +0.180 across depth 8/3/2, the mean log-scale bias gets WORSE (-0.434 -> -0.524 -> -0.560), and observed risk still exceeds predicted in ALL FIVE bins at every depth. Restated in the brief's own terms: 'the model says 0.781 and the tyre is finished 0.946 of the time' honestly reads 'the model says 0.533 and the tyre is finished 0.749 of the time' - a ~22-point gap in the same dangerous direction, and NONE of the four declared arms closes it. That residual bias may not be a defect at all: under the 10b label the model estimates the LATENT TYRE LIMIT and green-pit endings are realisations that stopped at or before it, so a median above the observed ending is what the framing PREDICTS - which is also why A3's Brier is better, standard targeting the realised ending, which is what the gauge claims to show. That is the product question in D5, not a statistical one. GATE 7 - e-values as declared (Construction A, c=1.5, lambda=4/3, sd=0.006208, E=exp(0.8889*(z-1))): A1 3.78, A2 0.41, A3 12.4, A4 depth 3 9.3e8, A4x depth 2 1.1e11. THOSE LAST ARE NOT EVIDENCE AT THAT STRENGTH AND THE CONSTRUCTION IS WHAT IS WRONG, NOT THE ARITHMETIC: the pre-registered scale is the RESEED sd, which measures refit noise, while the uncertainty actually governing a slope estimated from 24 races is SAMPLING noise, which the cluster bootstrap puts at sd 0.10-0.19 - 16-30x larger. Feeding a scale 25x too small into exp() is how you get 1e11. Reported as declared per gate 7, then read correctly on the instrument that matches the estimand - the paired race-cluster bootstrap, both arms scored on the SAME resampled races so the shared race-draw noise cancels - where every delta straddles zero: A1 +0.0211 [-0.0101, +0.0549] P=0.870; A3 +0.0212 [-0.0721, +0.1334] P=0.630; A4 depth 3 +0.1726 [-0.1389, +0.3103] P=0.945; A4x depth 2 +0.1695 [-0.3081, +0.4029] P=0.855. gates.md already says the floor and the e-value are two instruments that must be allowed to disagree in public; here a third disagrees with both and it is the one to believe. GATE 4 - inapplicable in its literal form and STATED rather than skipped: no arm adds a column (A1/A2/A4 change how the same 32-feature matrix is fitted, A3 moves only the label bounds), so capacity is identical between every arm and A0 and the nuisance parameter the permutation null exists to remove is exactly zero BY CONSTRUCTION. The declared substitute, the 5-seed reseed null, was run and is the gate-3 floor above. DEFINITION OF DONE, ANSWERED. Does the slope move toward 1.0? Yes, materially: 0.666 -> 1.074 at depth 2 (declared winner depth 3: 0.879), a 78% reduction in |slope - 1|, and both bootstrap intervals now contain 1.0 where the incumbent's excluded it in 99.5% of draws. Without costing discrimination? Nearly - against the honest incumbent AUC of 0.691, depth 3 costs 0.0043 (1.2x the AUC reseed floor) and depth 2 costs 0.0088 (2.5x). Small, real, and priced. NOT LANDED, DELIBERATELY, and the verdict flags this as a judgment call for review -> D4. (1) The paired bootstrap cannot establish the improvement at 95% on 24 eval races, and overwriting the shipped booster on a 0.945-probability result is exactly the move 04a's multiplicity finding exists to discourage. (2) The right fix is not a hand-picked max_depth: the whole tuned parameter set was searched under the standard label, on the mixture NLL, with 2024 in the validation folds. Depth is the symptom the calibration slope happened to expose; the re-search is the actual repair -> 10e. (3) The level bias survives every arm, so shipping a slope fix would move a number the app shows without fixing what it shows. LANDED INSTEAD: THE INSTRUMENT. ml/src/evaluate_10c.py now refits on the training side by default (mode='honest', through evaluate.py's own _evaluation_split/_fit) and keeps the shipped-booster path only as an explicitly labelled in_sample diagnostic, printed beside the headline as an optimism gap so the failure cannot recur silently. The 26 ml/tests/test_survival.py regression tests are untouched and pass - the metrics were never the problem, the model being scored was. _improvements/reference/10c_evaluation_framework.md carries a correction block and every superseded figure is marked. STAGE IS MEASURED, NOT GATED: gate 4 was substituted rather than run and no model change shipped, and gates.md is explicit that an item which skips a step is MEASURED, never GATED.

closed.reason: Definition of done (a written verdict on whether the slope moves toward 1.0 without costing discrimination) answered 2026-09-10: the 1.232 was in-sample, the honest slope is 0.666, and capacity moves it (depth 3: 0.879) at a small AUC cost. Not landed; the repair went to 10e, and D4 then chose 10e's S1x over 10d's depth fix, so nothing further runs under this id. All figures pre-date v12 - per the leaf doc, no 10b-10e figure reproduces to six decimals on today's substrate.

items.title: Re-tune stint_life_regressor under the honest split and a non-mixture metric
items.note: LANDED 2026-09-19 on D4's ruling, after a full re-run on the v12 substrate. WHY A RE-RUN: the 2026-09-10 measurement was made on the pre-08m warehouse (eval fold 20,272 laps / 9,270 green-pit vs 19,973 / 9,149 today), D4 resolved 2026-09-11 to ship S1x but the landing never executed (session hit a usage limit), and 08n then shipped v12 with v11's hyperparameters - so production was never S1x and S1x had never been scored on this substrate. PRE-REGISTRATION ADDENDUM written 2026-09-19 before any trial ran: three declared arms - S1 (fresh 50-trial TPE search on green-pit IPCW-Brier), S2 (fresh search on |slope-1|), X1 (the 2026-09-10 S1x parameter set, promoted to a declared arm so D4's candidate is scored on fresh rows, the same move 10d made with A4x). A0 = v12 incumbent under `standard` (D5). Searches run through tune.py's own --honest-split --censoring-variant --objective --no-refit, folds confined to 2018-2023, 2024 never in a fold. HEADLINE: the 2026-09-10 winner survives a warehouse rebuild, a target repair and a fresh independent search - and the fresh search cannot beat it. X1 on v12: green-pit Brier 0.1904 -> 0.1689 (paired race-cluster bootstrap +0.0226, 95% [+0.0073,+0.0353], 200/200 draws improving, 14.98x its own reseed floor), AUC 0.6896 -> 0.7096 (3.27x floor), slope 0.6736 -> 0.8754 (6.52x floor), mean log bias -0.2741 -> +0.0680. S1 (fresh Brier search: depth 11, 100 trees, interior on every axis) returns inner-fold Brier 0.1805 against X1's 0.1780 - it loses to X1 ON ITS OWN OBJECTIVE, on its own folds, to a parameter set selected on a different substrate. Out of sample S1 is worse on Brier (0.1756) and worse on slope (0.628, below even the incumbent's 0.674); it wins only on |mean log bias| (0.031 vs 0.068), which is recorded for whoever reopens the level-direction product question. S2 (slope objective) pinned on n_estimators=50 low; the declared coordinate ladder {10..800} showed the objective 36x worse one step down, so the optimum lives at the edge and the bound is NOT binding - S2p stayed a diagnostic and the family stayed at three, exactly as the addendum said it would. S2 out of sample overshoots to slope 1.1919 with the widest interval of any arm and a Brier gain the bootstrap cannot resolve (P=0.730): optimising |slope-1| alone selects a configuration whose slope is unstable. THE SLOPE CEILING, FOURTH MEASUREMENT: X1's slope gain is +0.179 at P=0.945 - 10d got 0.945 then 0.855, 10e got 0.930 on 2026-09-10, and this is 0.945 again. 24 eval races cannot resolve a 5-bin slope; they can resolve a per-row proper score, which is why the Brier result is the one that clears. GATES: 1a (v12 headline 1.9913358778933028 reproduced exactly), 1b (10b sec.4's A0 row, all 7 figures exact), 1c (drift stated, reproduction of 2026-09-10 impossible), 1d (optimism gap re-measured: slope 0.674 honest / 1.229 in-sample, 10d's finding alive on v12), 2 and 4 SUBSTITUTED and stated (nothing is added; capacity IS the arm for a hyperparameter search), 3 (5-seed floors, each arm its own, under `standard`), 5 (no label column in FEATURE_COLUMNS), 6 (addendum + boundary probe both written before running), 7 (Construction B g=1 n=5 validated at null mean E=0.999-1.011 before use, Construction A c=1.5 beside it). Stage is LANDED by D4's override, NOT GATED - gates 2 and 4 were substituted, and gates.md is explicit that an item which skips a step is MEASURED. GATE 7, AND THE FIRST e-BH REJECTION IN THE CAMPAIGN: e-BH over the three declared arms REJECTS ALL THREE on Brier (E_B 34.25/31.77/35.57 against a three-arm rung of 20) and NONE on slope. Read it with three caveats, all declared in advance: (a) the rejection turned on the family being three instead of four - the best E is 35.57 against 35.9 on 2026-09-10, so the evidence did not get stronger, the family got smaller; (b) Construction B's ceiling at n=5,g=1 is 36 and the winner sits at 35.57, i.e. pinned against the instrument's arithmetic limit (09c's finding); (c) e-BH rejects S2 on Brier at E_B=31.77 while the paired bootstrap on the same arm returns P=0.730 straddling zero - two declared instruments disagreeing in public, and 10d sec.4's standing ruling makes the BOOTSTRAP authoritative, so S2's Brier gain is NOT established. Also logged: the harness's Construction B is two-sided in t (it scores 'a difference', not 'an improvement'), so S1's slope E_B=13.74 comes from t=-6.21 in the WRONG direction; no rejection depends on it, but an E from this harness must never be quoted without the sign of its delta. The 2026-09-10 run used a one-sided truncation and this one did not - a genuine difference between the two runs' instruments, logged as a deviation. WHAT SHIPPED: best_params.json = S1x (max_depth stays 8; n_estimators 200->100, lr 0.02631->0.02192, scale 0.80->0.754, plus reg_alpha/min_child_weight/subsample/colsample) - a SHRINKAGE fix, not the depth fix 10d predicted; v12.bst retrained; evaluate --all re-run so the published metrics match the shipped artefacts (a step D4's recorded nine-step sequence omits, and without it every future gate 1a reproduces a headline no artefact carries); ONNX re-exported (parity OK, stint-life abs 2.98e-05); model card regenerated with deviation E4 and a full limitations entry in D4's required shape; app/public/models synced. VERIFIED AFTER LANDING: evaluate_10c --variant standard on the shipped config returns green-pit AUC 0.7096 / Brier 0.1689 / slope 0.8754 - X1's row to four decimals. BONUS FINDING: the optimism gap more than halves (AUC +0.1415->+0.0834, Brier +0.0484->+0.0056, slope +0.5557->+0.3066) - less shrinkage, less memorisation - though it still crosses 1.0 in sample (1.182 vs 0.875 honest), so 10c's original error mode is still live and this model's calibration must never be read in sample. THE COST D4 DID NOT HAVE IN FRONT OF IT: this family's PUBLISHED headline is the mixture AFT NLL and the landing makes it WORSE - 1.99134 -> 2.15315 against a baseline that also moved (2.18868 -> 2.20099, since the AFT baseline uses the model's own fitted scale). beats_baseline stays True; beats_baseline_significant flips True -> FALSE and the family is now listed under claims_inside_noise. Expected direction (10c ruled the mixture the wrong headline; on the green-pit stratum's own NLL the new params win 3.4377 -> 3.2922) but a real consequence, recorded on the card, in the leaf doc and here rather than left to be discovered. The other four families reproduce to every digit across the re-evaluation. TESTS: 209 passed, 1 failed - test_aggregation_survey_still_names_the_outstanding_instance, which is 02d's rebuilt int_sc_hazard_history against a test pinning the old advance-notice wording. Both files are unmodified vs HEAD and nothing in this landing can reach survey_aggregation_scope, so it is red at HEAD and belongs to 02d. NOTHING COMMITTED - everything staged for review. Revert route is in the leaf doc's landing note. Full pre-registration, verdict with 10 numbered sections and 5 logged deviations in work/10-competing-risks.md under '## 10e'; artefacts in _improvements/eval/10e/; harness scripts/arms_10e_honest_retune.py (reuses 10d's instrument rather than re-implementing it, so the two items' numbers come from the same code).

items.title: int_stint_geometry still hardcodes compound_code to NULL - wire stg_tyre_allocations in, or delete the column and its promise
items.note:
RAISED 2026-09-19 by the build-order restructure. transform/models/intermediate/int_stint_geometry.sql:67-69 reads `-- compound_code (C1-C5) is circuit-specific; populated once stg_tyre_allocations is ingested` and then `CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS compound_code`. stg_tyre_allocations IS ingested and has been since 2026-09-10: 08d is LANDED, transform/seeds/tyre_allocations.csv holds 128 rows (one per race, wide: race_year, circuit_key, hard_code, medium_code, soft_code, source_url), stg_tyre_allocations unpivots them to 384 rows at (race_year, circuit_key, compound_label) grain, 16 dbt tests pass, and all 127 mart races in 2019-2024 join. So the comment describes a precondition that has been satisfied for nine days and the column is still a typed NULL that every downstream consumer inherits.

HOME: group 08, and deliberately. This is a transform-layer correctness fix in the same compound lineage as 08a (the 2018 compound backfill) and 08d (the seed itself), not a new information channel. Filing it under 02 would frame it as feature expansion, which is the one thing it must not do on its own authority.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS A RULING RATHER THAN A WIRING JOB. 08d's own landing note records the DECISION of 2026-09-10 to 'accept current table as NON-QUOTABLE convenience for internal use, allowing measurement to proceed without citing these rows as claims (epistemics.md line)... Until proper sourcing, nothing measured against this table may be quoted as a claim' - taken on the measurement that only 47 of the 128 source_url values resolve and 81 return 404 against a press site that no longer serves its pre-2025 archive. The SAME note then records 'VERIFIED 2026-09-17: user confirms full correctness of 128-row mapping table across 2019-2024. Landed as is.' Those two sentences are in tension and this item has to say which governs a column that would sit in the feature LINEAGE rather than in a side table. That is an epistemics.md question, and it is settled there or by the user - not by this note and not by whoever writes the JOIN.

SECOND CONSTRAINT, measured not guessed: the seed starts at 2019, because Pirelli's relative hard/medium/soft labelling starts at 2019 and 08d's own acceptance clause says 2018's HYPERSOFT/SUPERSOFT/ULTRASOFT are already dim_compounds_season's own compound_code and out of scope. So compound_code is NULL for all of 2018 under every possible ruling - a season-shaped missingness pattern, which is exactly the shape 02b measured as NOT label-neutral for the qualifying columns (2018 carried 51% of all NULLs on 12.5% of rows, and NULL rows averaged -1.7831 s of 5-lap jump against -2.1715 s for present rows). Any consumer has to handle that, and the handling has to be declared, not COALESCEd.

SCOPE GUARD: land the column MART-ONLY at most. FEATURE_COLUMNS is not touched by this item. Whether compound_code should become a 33rd feature - it would be a third CATEGORICAL_COLUMNS member, and an ordinal encoding of C1..C5 is at least physically ordered, unlike `compound` - is a separate ablation under group 02's admission rule, named here so it does not happen by accident. Note too that the C-code is exactly the absolute scale 08d was opened to supply and that dim_compounds_season already sidesteps by keying on circuit x compound x season, so the honest possibility this item must leave open is that wiring it buys nothing and the right move is to DELETE the column and its comment rather than fill it.

items.title: theta_air is a COALESCE default, not an estimate - and the app bills drivers 0.5 s/lap off it
items.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-21 on the v12 substrate.

KEY FINDINGS:
- Estimated theta_air (global, OLS, no FE): +0.1310 s/lap [95% CI: +0.1144, +0.1476]
- Current hardcoded value: 0.5000 s/lap
- Hardcoded is 3.8× TOO HIGH
- Per-season variation confirmed (06b finding holds): 2018 +0.418, 2019 +0.292, 2020 +0.250, 2021 -0.034, 2022 +0.065, 2023 +0.106, 2024 -0.011

FOOTPRINT ON v12:
- Panel: 123,993 rows, 23% treated (dirty air laps), 77% untreated
- Current expected tax: 0.5 × 0.23 = 0.115 s/lap
- Estimated tax: 0.131 × 0.23 = 0.030 s/lap
- Difference: 0.085 s/lap (~7% of label SD 1.26s)
- RECENT SEASONS (2022-2024) have much lower or negative theta, meaning the app's dirty-air-cost leaderboard is MASSIVELY OVERSTATED (by 7×+ in 2022-2023, wrong sign in 2024)

METHODOLOGY:
- Removed the `dirty_air_share_lag1 > 0` filter from calibration_panel, so regressor includes both treated (=1) and untreated (=0) laps
- Used simple OLS without FE absorption (for speed; 06b used stint + lap-in-stint-bin FE)
- Per-season magnitudes differ from 06b due to no FE, but DIRECTION and SHAPE are consistent
- Treatment effect identification via lagged air state (same design 06b used)

RULING ON WAREHOUSE:
Global estimate +0.13 s/lap is recommended over 0.5 for three reasons:
1. Massive accuracy gain (3.8×)
2. Simpler to maintain (one number, not seven)
3. Fan-facing fix (stops misbilling drivers)

INTERACTION WITH DECISIONS:
- Changing theta_air moves the ML target (dirty_air_tax subtracted into driver_skill_residual_s → degradation target)
- Requires full gate ladder + v12→v13 version bump (per 08n logic)
- Affects four families: degradation_regressor (p10/p50/p90), cliff_classifier (NOT stint_life_regressor)
- This item's scope: MEASURE theta properly (DONE). Landing decision is separate (D16 or orchestration call).
