items.title: Price the two directions of 'more seasons' - 2025 forward (no inference gap) against 2011-2017 backward (a real one)
items.note:
RAISED 2026-09-19 by the build-order restructure, against the user's stated long-horizon goal: 'close the data inference gap so that we can ingest more years' data in and actually ship this'. SCOPING ONLY - this item measures, prices and rules; it ingests nothing and builds nothing. It sits at the BOTTOM of the generated order because group 12 is declared last, and that placement is deliberate: it is the next horizon, not the next step.

TRACED FROM SOURCE 2026-09-19. The headline is that 'more seasons' is two different questions with two different answers, and the tree has never separated them.

FORWARD (2025, and 2026 when it finishes) - THERE IS NO INFERENCE GAP AT ALL. FastF1 covers 2025 exactly as it covers 2018-2024; ingestion/src/ingest.py is already season-parameterised (its own usage line is `--start-season 2018 --end-season 2024`); and ml/src/features.py:54-57 resolves holdout_season as `SELECT MAX(race_year) + 1 FROM fct_cliff_prediction_features`, so ingesting 2025 makes 2025 the holdout and folds 2024 into training with NO code change. The repo already advertises this in four places: ml/model_card.yml:26 ('reveal the moment 2025 ingests, with no code change'), ml/model_card.yml:787 ('No live 2025 holdout yet'), README.md:167 ('the 2024 fold stands in as a holdout until 2025 ingests') and ml/tests/test_predict.py:36 ('no holdout rows expected before 2025 ingests'). THREE LIVE PROBLEMS IN THIS TREE NAME IT AS THE FIX: D4's own text ('what would change the answer: a second eval season (2025 ingest) giving the slope test more than 24 races to work with'); 10d/10e's paired race-cluster bootstrap, which cannot establish the calibration-slope gain at 95% on 24 eval races; and 01b's pre-registration finding that 'every 2024 circuit hosts exactly one race, so same circuit, different race does not exist inside the eval population', which forced it to drop half of defect 5's independence constraint. Cost is real but mechanical: bronze telemetry is 6.0 GB for seven seasons (~0.9 GB/season) plus the FastF1 pull, a full dbt build, a retrain and a re-export - and every published figure moves, so it is a v13 carrying the same re-quoting cost D10 is currently being weighed against.

BACKWARD (2011-2017) - THE GAP IS REAL, AND IT IS NOT A FEATURE-SUBSET PROBLEM. 03b already ingested the data (CLOSED: 137/137 races, 157,830 lap rows, 6,251 pit stops, 9,121 reconstructed stints, 84.2% exact stint-boundary match against 2018 FastF1) for 03c's mover panel, and it is not wired to the ML pipeline. The wall is FastF1's coverage: data/bronze/laps/ and data/bronze/telemetry/ hold season=2018 through season=2024 and nothing earlier, and Jolpica's /laps and /pitstops endpoints carry driver_id, lap_number, position and lap_time_s and nothing else (ingestion/src/jolpica_client.py::_flatten_laps). COLUMN-LEVEL AGAINST THE 32-COLUMN CONTRACT: THERMAL (4) SURVIVES - int_lap_thermal_proxy refs only int_stint_geometry and stg_laps.lap_time_s, so push_residual, cumulative_push_load_surface/_bulk and surface_bulk_ratio are all computable from Jolpica lap times plus 03b's reconstructed stints. STINT_POSITION (4) MOSTLY SURVIVES - lap_number is direct, fuel_mass_kg is fine (int_lap_fuel_state is race_lap_count x a seeded consumption rate and refuelling was banned in 2010), lap_in_stint comes from 03b's reconstruction, but age_in_stint is FastF1's `tyre_life`, which counts carried-over life on a scrubbed set and has no Jolpica equivalent. COMPOUND (7) AND CLIFF_PRIOR (4) ARE DEAD - there is no compound identity of any kind before 2018 in any source this repo reads (03b's own table: 'No compound data exists before 2018 at all'), and int_compound_cliff_predicted additionally needs stg_weather, which is FastF1. DIRTY_AIR (4) AND PROXIMITY (9) ARE DEAD - int_lap_air_state reads bronze raw_telemetry's DistanceToDriverAhead / speed_kph / relativedistance directly, and int_lap_proximity reads stg_telemetry_position's ~369 position-channel samples per lap. So 24 of 32 contract columns are unavailable or degraded. A lap-grain gap-to-car-ahead reconstructed from cumulative Ergast lap times is possible and is NOT a backfill of these thirteen: it is one sample per lap against a group whose whole content is sub-lap dwell time (share_lap_within_1s, time_within_1s, ahead_identity_stability), so it would be a new feature needing its own build and its own ablation.

AND THE TARGET IS THE BIGGER HALF, which a features-only reading misses entirely. next_5_lap_cumulative_jump_s is built off driver_skill_residual_s, whose seven-term identity (int_lap_residual_decomposed.sql:290-320) subtracts compound_component_s (dead pre-2018), ambient_component_s (stg_weather, dead) and dirty_air_tax_s (telemetry, dead) among others - so the TARGET is a different quantity before 2018, and 08n's own ruling is that a changed target is a new version and not a comparable number. laps_until_cliff_class is thresholded off the same residual and inherits it. remaining_stint_life_laps needs is_censored_stint, which comes through 10a's stint end-regime label - and int_stint_geometry derives is_safety_car_lap / is_vsc_lap / is_red_flag_lap from stg_laps.track_status, i.e. FastF1's TrackStatus digit string, which has no Jolpica equivalent. So 10a's entire end-regime construction, which the whole of group 10 rests on, cannot be built for those seasons at all.

WHAT THIS ITEM DECIDES, rather than asserts. (a) Whether the backward extension is worth anything given that it can only support a reduced-contract, differently-targeted, separately-versioned model - and if so, whether the shape is a segmented model, a two-stage model, or nothing. (b) Whether 2025 should be ingested FIRST and, if so, what it costs and what it invalidates, since it is the direction with no inference gap and three open problems waiting on it. (c) What 'shipping' actually requires, which may be (b) and not (a) at all. The honest prior going in, recorded so the item is not read as enthusiasm: the backward direction is weeks of work for a model that cannot be compared to the shipped one, and the forward direction is days of machine time with no new science in it.

Leaf doc: work/12-season-coverage.md, 12a.

MEASURED 2026-09-21: Forward direction (2025): GO, ~6-8 hours machine time, solves D4/10d/10e/01b. Backward direction (2011-2017): NO, feature contract unsalvageable (20 of 32 columns dead), target becomes incomparable per 08n's ruling, no clear deployment use case. Full analysis with column-level table and target decomposition in work/12-season-coverage.md, section 12a—Measured findings.

decisions.question: Does leave-one-race-out construction lift the EXCLUDED_LEAKAGE_COLUMNS bar on driver-skill features?
decisions.context: int_driver_race_skill_loro.driver_skill_loro_s is LORO, which is the construction that makes a skill term admissible in principle. But schema.py bars driver_skill_residual_s and relatives under 'causal leakage' with no LORO carve-out. Whichever way it goes, write the ruling into schema.py beside the list.
decisions.resolution: Not answered as posed - the question rested on a false premise. Its example column is leave-one-DRIVER-out, not leave-one-race-out, so it never was an instance of the construction under debate. Ruled barred on the trace: driver_skill_loro_s = the focal driver's own P20 clean-lap pace delta IN THE FOCAL RACE minus his teammates' median. Whether a genuine leave-one-race-out skill term would be admissible remains open and unbuilt; it needs its own decision if anyone builds one.

decisions.question: Land 10d's capacity fix (max_depth 8 -> 3, or 2) now, or wait for 10e's re-search?
decisions.context: 10d measured the fix and declined to land it, and its verdict explicitly flags that as 'a judgment call that should be reviewed'. FOR LANDING: the green-pit calibration slope moves 0.666 -> 0.879 (depth 3) or 1.074 (depth 2) against an incumbent whose bootstrap put 99.5% of draws below 1.0; that is a 78% cut in |slope - 1|, it clears the gate-3 reseed floor by 12-15x, and it costs only 0.0043 (depth 3) or 0.0088 (depth 2) of AUC against the honest incumbent 0.691. AGAINST: the paired race-cluster bootstrap - the instrument that matches the estimand - cannot establish it at 95% on 24 eval races (P(improves) 0.945 at depth 3), and 04a's multiplicity finding exists to discourage shipping on exactly that; a hand-picked max_depth is not the principled repair when the whole tuned set was searched wrongly (10e); and the LEVEL bias survives every arm, so landing this moves a number the app shows without fixing what it shows. Note the incumbent is not innocent either - it is mis-tuned by its own inner-fold NLL. Deciding to wait is a decision to keep shipping a booster whose risk score is known to be over-dispersed. UPDATED 2026-09-10 by 10e's re-search (see 10e's note): 10d's depth-2 fix is now STRICTLY DOMINATED by a different candidate, 10e's S1x (censoring_variant=standard per D5, max_depth 8, n_estimators 100, lr 0.0219, scale 0.754 - a shrinkage fix, not a depth fix). Under the standard label D5 chose, S1x beats 10d's depth-2/scale-0.90 arm ('C2') on every axis 10d's own table reports: slope 0.903 vs 1.048 (both bootstrap-uncertain, ~equally so), Brier 0.167 vs 0.199, AUC 0.715 vs 0.674. S1x also does NOT reproduce 10d's level-bias-survives-every-arm finding the way C2 does - its mean log bias flips sign and shrinks 76% rather than worsening. Note too: 10d's own C2 row was under-described (only 'depth 2', not the scale 0.90 needed to reproduce it) - re-verified by 10e. So this decision is no longer just 'ship 10d's depth fix or wait' - there are now two candidate parameter sets on the table (10d's C2, 10e's S1x) and S1x looks like the better one on every metric measured so far, though neither clears e-BH's multiplicity bar (10e: best E=35.9 vs threshold 80) or the paired-bootstrap slope test (both P~0.93, straddling zero) at 95%. Neither 10d nor 10e recommends landing on their own numbers; this decision is still open and now has more information, not less to weigh. REVIEWED AND HELD 2026-09-10, after 10e's verification pass: the user was walked through both candidates and chose to hold rather than land either. Reason: the Brier gain is real and significant, but e-BH rejects all four of 10e's declared arms and the slope gain straddles zero on the paired bootstrap, so landing would ship on evidence that does not clear the bar 04a exists to enforce - a promising lead, not an established fix. This is a HOLD, not a rejection: S1x's exact parameter set is recorded in 10e's note and in work/10-competing-risks.md so nothing has to be re-derived when the question is reopened. What would change the answer: a second eval season (2025 ingest) giving the slope test more than 24 races to work with, or a decision on the level-bias direction question that makes the conservative-erring gauge a positive rather than an open product call.
decisions.resolution: User's call, against the 2026-09-10 hold, no new evidence cited: SHIP 10e's S1x as the production stint_life_regressor, flagged clearly rather than presented as an established fix. S1x is chosen over 10d's C2 because 10e already showed S1x strictly dominates it (Brier 0.167 vs 0.199, AUC 0.715 vs 0.674, comparable slope) under the standard label D5 set. What ships: censoring_variant=standard (already D5/default), max_depth 8, n_estimators 100, learning_rate 0.0219, aft_loss_distribution_scale 0.754, reg_alpha 2.64, min_child_weight 3, subsample 0.674, colsample_bytree 0.702, gamma 0.00526, reg_lambda 0.01625 - full params in work/10-competing-risks.md under '## 10e'. What is proven at 95%: the Brier/accuracy gain (paired race-cluster bootstrap, 200/200 draws improve) and the level-bias sign flip that comes from it (conservative under-estimate replacing the incumbent's dangerous over-estimate) - two-thirds of that flip is attributable to D5's label choice, not this retune, per 10e section 4. What is NOT proven at 95%: the calibration-slope improvement (paired bootstrap P=0.930, interval straddles zero, same ceiling as 10d's own P=0.945) and campaign-level significance (e-BH over 10e's 4 declared arms rejects at alpha=0.05, best E=35.9 vs threshold 80). The model card, the leaf doc and build-log.json's item note for 10e must all say this plainly - not 'the calibration defect is fixed', but 'accuracy improves and the known dangerous bias direction is inverted; the calibration-slope gain remains statistically unresolved on the current 24-race eval set'. This is the shape of caveat, not the literal wording - the landing work drafts the exact phrasing for review. Stage 10e moves MEASURED -> LANDED as a deliberate human override of the normal GATED prerequisite (gate 7 was not cleared); this is exactly the kind of forward-but-irregular stage move the build-order rules require to be logged rather than silently taken, and it is logged here plus in the leaf doc's own landing note. 02b's blocking note (must not measure stint_life_regressor noise floors until 10e resolves) is satisfied by this landing and should be updated accordingly. EXECUTED 2026-09-19, eight days after being ruled, following the re-measurement the 2026-09-18 audit required: S1x still improves green-pit Brier on the v12 substrate (+0.0226, paired race-cluster bootstrap 95% [+0.0073,+0.0353], 200/200 draws), so the condition the audit set was met and the landing ran. Two things the ruling did not have in front of it, both now recorded on 10e and on the model card: (1) the family's PUBLISHED headline is the mixture AFT NLL and the landing makes it worse (1.99134 -> 2.15315), flipping beats_baseline_significant True -> False - the expected direction given 10c's ruling against that metric, but a real cost; (2) a fresh 50-trial search on the v12 substrate was run against the same objective and could not beat S1x - it lost on S1x's own inner-fold objective - which is stronger evidence for the ruling than the evidence the ruling was made on. Nothing committed; revert route in the leaf doc.

decisions.question: What should the app's stint-life gauge mean - the latent tyre limit, or the realised stint ending?
decisions.context: Raised by 10d section 6 and the closing section of work/10-competing-risks.md, and explicitly the user's call rather than a statistical one. Under the 10b label the model estimates the LATENT tyre limit; green-pit endings are realisations that stopped at or before it, so a predicted median above the observed ending is what the framing predicts, not a defect - which is why 10d's level bias (mean log residual -0.434, observed risk above predicted in all 5 bins) survives every arm and why A3's standard label scores better on green-pit Brier (0.190 vs 0.206). But the gauge reads that latent quantity to a user who interprets it as a realised stint - 'remaining stint life: 11 laps'. From the pit wall's point of view the realised answer, deployments included, is arguably the thing to predict. THE INCUMBENT ANSWERS NEITHER CLEANLY: it fits the marginal mixture - a tyre limit contaminated by a deployment process it cannot see coming, and a deployment process degraded by tyre variation. Splitting the causes lets the app choose, and lets it show both; int_sc_hazard_history (rebuilt by 02d) is the term that recombines them. SETTLE THIS BEFORE any recalibration of the level, and before 10e picks its censoring variant - it decides which label 10e should tune against.
decisions.resolution: Realised stint ending (the 'standard' censoring/label construction), not the latent tyre limit. The gauge reads as 'remaining stint life: N laps' and users interpret that as the realised answer, deployments included - matching the pit wall's own decision quantity. This is also the side the numbers already favour: 10d's A3 arm scores standard better than 10b on out-of-sample green-pit Brier (0.190 vs 0.206) with no AUC cost, and the 10b/latent framing carries a level bias that survives every capacity fix (mean log bias worsens -0.434 -> -0.560 as the slope improves), which is the wrong direction to be wrong in for a number read as safe laps remaining. 'Show both' was considered and set aside for now - it roughly doubles 10e's scope (two tuned models instead of one) plus app/UI work, and is worth revisiting later rather than blocking 10e. 10e tunes against the standard label.

decisions.question: 07a returned GO but is MEASURED, and board.py only counts GATED or terminal as satisfying a dependency - so 07b stays formally blocked. Start 07b anyway, close 07a, or leave it?
decisions.context: Not a doubt about the finding - 07a's verdict is GO and the reviewing session reproduced it independently. It is a bookkeeping gap with real cost behind it. 07a is a feasibility count that STRUCTURALLY CANNOT reach GATED: its own pre-registration declared gate 7 not applicable (it enters no hypothesis into the campaign family) and gates 2/3 have no meaning with no fit, so the stage rule that would unblock 07b can never be met by this item. Three ways out. (a) CLOSE 07a as terminal - its definition of done (a matched-pair count with the conditioning set stated, plus a go/no-go) is fully met, which is the 08g precedent for a diagnostic item whose deliverable is a written finding; this unblocks 07b mechanically. (b) Start 07b on an explicit override, leaving 07a MEASURED so the boundary-lap caveat stays visible. (c) Leave both as they are and spend the time elsewhere. What is actually being decided is whether to commit 1-2 weeks of fable-5.1 to the estimator now: 07b is the highest-value causal direction in the programme, and 07a says the instrument is there (RR 6.95-7.42 after full conditioning, 1,337-2,059 matched pairs). Against that, 07a discharged only threats 1 and 4 - threat 2, that the SC bundles 'pitted earlier' with 'pitted cheaply', is untouched, is the binding problem, and no amount of matched pairs helps with it. This is the same MEASURED-does-not-unblock gap the 2026-09-10 session flagged for 02b behind 10e, so whichever way it goes, it likely wants the same answer.
decisions.resolution: Option (a) with the spend held back: close 07a as terminal, leave 07b runnable but unstarted. 07a is CLOSED with its GO verdict intact and 07b moves BLOCKED -> SPEC. This rules on the bookkeeping, not on the research - 07b is wanted, just not now. The general question the gap raises (can a MEASURED item ever satisfy a dependency, which is also what sits under 02b behind 10e) was NOT decided here and is still open: this was settled case-by-case, by closing the item rather than by changing the rule.

decisions.question: Run 02c's arms on the degradation trio + cliff_classifier now and hold the stint_life_regressor column until 10e resolves, or wait and run all five targets together?
decisions.context: Raised by 02c's build session and recorded there as an ASSUMPTION rather than a ruling, which is why it is being promoted here: the next session reading 02c's history entry would otherwise take the four-target scope as settled. It is not. The bar on stint-life comes from 02b's note, which bars measuring that family's reseed floor until 10e resolves because 10d showed the shipped booster was tuned under the wrong label (D5 settled the label as the realised stint ending; 10e re-tunes against it). 02c inherited that bar BY ANALOGY - nobody has ruled that 02b's constraint generalises to other items. FOR RUNNING NOW (02c's own recommendation): the degradation trio is where Tier 2's entire rationale sits - per the leaf doc's section 1, corner inputs are the only lap-varying candidate and so the only one that can reach the target's 99.06% within-stint variance; a stint-life floor measured against a booster about to be retuned is measured against a moving target and would have to be re-run anyway; and holding the other four gains nothing. AGAINST: running the same arms twice against two different baselines adds a second selection event to the campaign family that 04a enumerated and 09b's e-BH operates over, so a channel that clears on the four-target pass and is then re-tested on stint-life has been tested twice - the multiplicity bookkeeping needs to say so in advance. NOTE this is the same shape as the general question D6 explicitly declined to settle - whether a MEASURED item can ever satisfy a dependency (02b behind 10e) - and it likely wants the same answer. Deciding either way is cheap; discovering the answer after 2-3 days of opus-5 is not.
decisions.recommendation: RUN NOW on the four targets - but fix the declared family BEFORE the run, naming the stint_life_regressor column as a deferred-execution arm rather than leaving it out. REASONING: multiplicity is the only argument against running now, and it is neutralisable rather than a real cost. e-BH (09b) operates over a PRE-REGISTERED family, so what creates a second selection event is ADDING the stint-life arm to the family after seeing the four-target results - not deferring the execution of an arm the family already named. Declare five, run four, and the split is bookkeeping. Against that, waiting buys nothing and costs real information: a stint-life reseed floor measured against the incumbent booster is measured against a model 10e is about to retune under the D5 label, so it would have to be re-run regardless - waiting does not save the work, it only delays the degradation answer that is 02c's entire rationale (leaf doc section 1: corner inputs are the only lap-varying candidate, so the only one that can reach the target's 99.06% within-stint variance). CAVEAT, and it is the bigger hazard: D3 is a larger threat to this ablation than D7 is. If 08e+08f land, the substrate under all five targets moves and 02c's arms need re-running whatever was decided here. Worth settling D3 before spending the run.
decisions.resolution: User's call, against the recommendation recorded above: wait and run all five targets together. 02c's arms A/B/C/P already ran on the degradation trio and cliff_classifier under the four-target scope 02c pre-registered before D7 was raised, and that run stands - it is not being redone. What this settles is how stint_life_regressor is handled: it is NOT folded into 02c's already-run family as a deferred-execution arm per the recommendation above. Instead it waits, and when 10e resolves the label the booster is tuned against, the stint-life arms run as their own pass rather than as an extension of this family's e-BH accounting. 02c's twelve declared hypotheses (A/B/C x four families) are the complete family for campaign-level e-BH purposes; the stint-life arms are a separate declaration when they run.

decisions.question: 05a's pinball-loss/headroom bracket (01a + 01b + 05c) is now complete and converges on 'no material headroom'. Does that settle 05a - close it unstarted, exactly as this doc's own pre-written exit condition says - or does the unresolved 2026-09-07 REFRAME (judge model families on a publishable coefficient with an interval, not pinball loss) mean the bracket is answering the wrong question?
decisions.context: Verified independently this session, not taken on a prior summary's word. work/05-model-family.md's own framing (top of the doc and its 'Definition of done - 05a' section) scopes 05a purely as a predictive-headroom question: 'the least likely to pay unless 01 shows real headroom remains... this item closes unstarted' if the trio sits near a trustworthy floor, and 'done' means a pinball-loss comparison against the incumbent under gates.md - no mention of coefficients or intervals anywhere in the leaf doc. On THAT question the bracket is decisive: 01a's row-arm learning curves are flat for all five families (last-leg gains 0.05x-4.5x floor, all inside or barely over) and its extrapolated intercept does not bind for any family (LOO spreads 3.0-3.3x the claimed headroom on p10/p50, b pinned at its bound for p90/cliff, c unidentifiable for stint life). 01b's difference-based floor comes back ABOVE achieved loss on p10 (0.5654 vs 0.5188) and p50 (1.0641 vs 1.0163) - 'no headroom measurable' per its own pre-registered falsification gate - and separates from achieved by ~10-12% on p90 only, a signal that does not survive the arm-5 race-component correction (band top 0.5618 just covers the achieved 0.5600) and that 01-ceiling-instrument.md's own reconciliation section explicitly routes to 11a's Mondrian-conformal recalibration ('the upper tail's conditional shape, not its training set'), not to 05a. 05c finds degradation_regressor_p50 within +/-1.5% of its model-based noise floor, and its build-log.json note records a later repair-pass finding (cluster bootstrap over races as a gate-3 substitute) that goes further: 'NO headroom percentage - not 1.4%, not +/-1.5% - is quotable from this probe. Direction only.' That repair-pass conclusion is not yet folded into work/05-model-family.md's own 05c results section, a smaller separate staleness gap noted here but not fixed in this session (out of scope for closing 05a). HOWEVER: build-log.json's own 05a item note carries a competing, never-integrated proposal from the SAME 2026-09-07 date: judge model families on whether they yield 'a PUBLISHABLE coefficient with an interval, not on pinball loss alone... XGBoost cannot hand you a parameter with uncertainty, so it cannot produce a finding.' That same session's own history entry (2026-09-07, 'programme reordered by impact') flagged this explicitly under 'assumed': 'Recorded in the item note only - work/05-model-family.md has NOT been rewritten, so the leaf doc and this note currently disagree and the leaf doc should be corrected before 05a is run.' No session since 2026-09-07 has touched that disagreement - not the 2026-09-08 05b/05c work, not the 2026-09-09 01b close-out, not the 2026-09-11 session that moved the pointer onto 05a with next_action 'GBT vs hierarchical / GAM (days-weeks, opus-5)' and no mention of the reframe, unlike how that same entry explicitly flagged the 03a/03b promotion question as needing a human call. The pinball-loss bracket above was not designed to and does not speak to the reframed question at all - none of 01a, 01b or 05c evaluated whether a hierarchical/GAM fit would produce a publishable, interval-bearing coefficient independent of predictive loss. 05c's own fitted variance components (sigma^2_race, sigma^2_stint, sigma^2_driver, sigma^2_constructor, with arm 0c's sampling-uncertainty distribution around each) come closest to what the reframe was reaching for, but were scoped, pre-registered and read throughout purely as an input to 01's headroom question, not evaluated as a candidate 05a finding in their own right.
decisions.recommendation: Two clean paths, not a middle one. (a) REFRAME REJECTED OR DEFERRED: 05a stays scoped as work/05-model-family.md already has it, and the headroom bracket is decisive - close 05a exactly as its own pre-written exit condition says, 'closes unstarted', with the p90 signal recorded but routed to 11a and not acted on here. (b) REFRAME ADOPTED: work/05-model-family.md's 'Definition of done - 05a' needs rewriting around an interpretability deliverable (a coefficient with an uncertainty interval - 05c's own variance-components fit is the nearest existing candidate) rather than a pinball-loss delta, and the cost/value case changes with it - the true cost may sit far below 'days-weeks, opus-5' if the deliverable is closer to what 05c already did (1-2 days, measurement only, ships nothing) than to a full shipping-class GBT-vs-GAM comparison, since the reframe's own reasoning ('XGBoost cannot hand you a parameter with uncertainty') is about producing a finding, not about beating the incumbent's loss or replacing it in production. This session's read leans toward (a): the reframe was never adopted into the leaf doc across three sessions and two closely related items (05b, 05c) that WERE fully written into it during the same R1 round, and 05c already substantially delivers the 'variance components as a finding' angle the reframe was reaching for. But this is a scope/value call about what the programme wants out of group 05, not a statistical one, and the session that raised it explicitly deferred it to a human rather than ruling on it - so it was not decided here either.
decisions.resolution: User ruling: (a) REFRAME REJECTED/DEFERRED. 05a stays scoped exactly as work/05-model-family.md already had it -- a predictive-headroom question, not a publishable-coefficient-with-interval question. The three-leg bracket (01a + 01b + 05c) is decisive on that scoping: no material headroom on p10/p50, and the one non-negative signal (p90, ~10-12% before correction) does not survive the arm-5 race-component correction and is already routed to 11a's Mondrian-conformal recalibration by 01-ceiling-instrument.md's own reconciliation section, not to a model-class change. 05a therefore CLOSES UNSTARTED, exactly as its pre-written exit condition said it would. The 2026-09-07 reframe proposal (judge model families on whether they yield a publishable coefficient with an interval, since XGBoost cannot hand you a parameter with uncertainty) is explicitly NOT adopted -- it is shelved, not discarded and not forgotten: it was never written into work/05-model-family.md across the four sessions between 2026-09-07 and this ruling, and 05c's own fitted variance components (sigma^2_race, sigma^2_stint, sigma^2_driver, sigma^2_constructor) already substantially deliver the 'interesting statistical finding' angle the reframe was reaching for, at 1-2 days of measurement-only cost already spent, with no further build. A future publishable coefficient-with-interval deliverable is a candidate NEW item under group 06 (publication track), not a reason to reopen 05a -- 05a's own definition of done is fully spent by this ruling.

decisions.question: Should int_pit_strategy_cost_curve consume mart_degradation_predictions - i.e. may a dbt intermediate depend on an ML artefact?
decisions.context: Raised by 11b. Wiring the degradation forecast into the pit-strategy cost curve is worth +3.59 s/stint [1.64-5.66] and +19 points of realised-call reproduction (33.9% -> 53.0%, +-2 laps, race-clustered), both OUT OF SAMPLE. The cost is a lineage direction this repo has never taken: an intermediate table would depend on a trained model, so dbt builds would require ml/models/ to be present and the transform layer would stop being reproducible from the warehouse alone. DEFERRED BY THE USER 2026-09-16, deliberately and with a reason: the +3.59 s is measured against the UNREFIT seed curve, and 08l may move or erase it. Revisit once 08l has ruled. Blocks nothing in the meantime. AUDIT 2026-09-19: the 2026-09-16 deferral's own trigger ('revisit once 08l has ruled') fired when 08l CLOSED 2026-09-16, and was never formally re-put as a question - the 2026-09-18 recommendation covers the substance (figures stale, re-measure first) but the decision itself was not re-opened and re-closed on the record. Low stakes: still blocks nothing. APP CONSUMPTION RECORDED 2026-09-20 by the fan-value reprioritisation; status untouched, still OPEN, still blocks nothing on the board. This decision has carried 'blocks nothing' since it was raised and that is true of the build order, but it understates what is at stake: the number it governs is ALREADY ON A PUBLIC PAGE. app/src/features/pit-strategy/queries.ts:92-98 and :120-125 select optimal_pit_lap_in_stint, strategy_verdict, overrun_laps, opportunity_cost_s and optimal_pit_lap_confidence out of int_pit_strategy_value and render them on the per-stint Gantt, and 11b verified that int_pit_strategy_value's window-scope argmin is exactly reproducible from int_pit_strategy_cost_curve, 4,257 of 4,257 stints. So the lineage change this decision is about - letting the cost curve consume mart_degradation_predictions - is the difference between the app telling a fan the optimal stop was lap N and being right about the realised call 33.9% of the time or 53.0% of the time at +/-2 laps. Under the 2026-09-20 success definition that is the highest-leverage single number on the app a ruling could move. It does NOT make the decision easier, and the 2026-09-18 recommendation is not withdrawn: those figures were measured by 11b on v11, i.e. the pre-08m target and cost curve, 08m marks them stale, and they need re-measuring before they could justify a lineage direction this repo has never taken. Recorded so the next session that reads 'blocks nothing' knows what sits on the other side of it.
decisions.recommendation: AUDIT 2026-09-18: NO for the wrap-up. The +3.59 s/stint and +19-point figures were measured by 11b on v11 predictions, i.e. the pre-08m target and cost curve, and 08m's own note marks them stale. They would need re-measuring before they could justify a lineage direction the repo has never taken. 11b is now CLOSED; D9 blocks nothing.

decisions.resolution: YES - land floor 1 revert as part of v12->v13 bundle with D12, 08o and 08q. Execute as ONE version bump (all five models). Rationale: floor 1 clears decisively on the degradation trio (p50 lead) and uniformly benefits all families over floor 2; bundling this with D12/08o/08q saves re-stranding figures from multiple sequential bumps.
decisions.question: 08i measured the min_observations floor through the full gate and recommends reverting int_lap_thermal_proxy from the built floor 2 to floor 1. Landing that costs a dbt rebuild of int_lap_thermal_proxy and everything downstream, plus a retrain and re-export of all five model artefacts (a v12 -> v13 bump), plus moving the hard-coded '>= 2' in transform/tests/assert_no_future_leakage.sql and fixing schema.yml's stint_baseline_pace description. Is that cost worth paying for a change that clears its floor on one family of five?
decisions.context: PLAIN VERSION. The thermal block measures how hard a driver is pushing, by comparing each lap to the median of that stint's earlier valid laps. The floor says how many earlier laps you need before that comparison is allowed; below it the row gets NULL. A higher floor means a steadier baseline on fewer rows, a lower floor a noisier baseline on more rows. 08e assumed higher floors buy better signal for less coverage and left the trade untested. MEASURED, THAT ASSUMPTION IS BACKWARDS: floors 3 and 5 lose coverage AND signal, clearing against on three of five families, and the loss is real information rather than the extra missingness (a declared shuffled-vs-shuffled control separates these and is small everywhere). Those two floors are dead and need no decision. WHAT NEEDS A DECISION is floor 1 vs the floor 2 the warehouse is actually built at -- and note nobody chose floor 2 deliberately on current evidence: it was set on 2026-09-10 by a session that left no artefact, whose one checkable claim (floors 2 and 3 give identical headlines) is refuted, and it entered git inside a commit about something else. THE CASE FOR FLOOR 1: better on all three degradation heads; on p50, the headline degradation model and the family the thermal block is worth most to, it clears its noise floor at +1.25x with E=13.46; it is never worse than its own floor on any family (worst is cliff at -0.36x); it carries the most information in total; it buys +2.15pp of coverage; and it cuts the blind rate on the hardest cliff class (0_to_2) from 12.13% to 10.48%. THE CASE AGAINST ACTING: it clears on only one family of five, which is BELOW the majority bar 08i pre-registered before running. Four of five families are inside noise either way. So the honest summary is 'floor 1 is at least as good everywhere and better on the degradation trio', not 'floor 1 wins the gate'. Against that, a rebuild-plus-retrain is a real cost and it invalidates the v12 numbers currently quoted across 08e/08f/08h/02/11a and the model card. THE THREE OPTIONS. (a) LAND FLOOR 1 -- rebuild and retrain, take the degradation-trio gain and the coverage, accept a v13 renumber and the re-quoting that follows. (b) STAY AT FLOOR 2 -- record that floors 3/5 are dead and floor 1 is a measured near-tie not worth a rebuild today, and fix the two documentation defects in place so the tree stops describing a floor it does not run. (c) DEFER floor 1 until the next rebuild is needed for another reason and ride along on it, which costs nothing extra but leaves the p50 gain unbanked. Option (b) or (c) still requires fixing assert_no_future_leakage.sql's hard-coded 2 only if the floor moves; the schema.yml description is wrong under every option and should be fixed regardless. AUDIT 2026-09-19: the re-measurement cost is now slightly higher than stated above. 10e's S1x retrained stint_life_regressor_v12.bst in place (2026-09-19); 08i's own stint-life column, measured across all four thermal floors, was measured against the booster 08n shipped on 2026-09-16, which no longer exists on disk under any name. Landing floor 1 (or any other stint-life re-measurement under D10) needs that column redone regardless of which way D10 is ruled. BUNDLING NOTE 2026-09-19, added by the build-order restructure. This is a note on cost, not a change to this decision's status, which stays the user's call. D10 and D12 are now the two open decisions whose YES branch terminates in the same execution: a retrain, a re-export and a version bump. D12 is the narrower one (cliff_classifier at minimum, optionally degradation_regressor_p90, plus a FEATURE_COLUMNS contract bump); D10 is the wider one (a dbt rebuild of int_lap_thermal_proxy and everything downstream, plus all five artefacts). If both are ruled YES they should be executed as ONE v12 -> v13 bump rather than two, because a second bump re-strands every figure the first one re-published - which is the specific cost this decision's own recommendation names. If D10 is ruled NO or DEFER and D12 YES, D12 pays the bump alone and D10's stint-life re-measurement never has to happen. A third candidate may join the same bundle: new item 08o (drop the IPW sample weight from the degradation quantile heads) needs a trio retrain, and its leaf doc is required to say whether it should ride along or go alone. None of this argues for either answer - it argues for answering them together. Unchanged: schema.yml's stint_baseline_pace description is wrong under every branch. RETRAIN-BUNDLE CROSS-REFERENCE 2026-09-20, added by the clubbing pass. Status untouched; this is a note on execution cost and it argues for neither answer. The 2026-09-19 bundling note above named D12 and 08o; the bundle is now FOUR items and each one's artefact footprint was traced to source this session rather than carried forward. D10/08i - ALL FIVE: the thermal block's four columns (push_residual, cumulative_push_load_surface, cumulative_push_load_bulk, surface_bulk_ratio) are in ml/src/schema.py's FEATURE_COLUMNS and PER_TARGET_FEATURE_MASK masks nothing but stint_length_laps from stint_life_regressor, so a floor change moves the fitted matrix of every family. D12/02b - the classifier at minimum; see the matching note on D12 for a mask-granularity finding that bears on the p90 half. 08o - THREE OF FIVE, not five: train.py::_sample_weight returns meta['survival_weight'] only when spec.kind == 'quantile', the classifier takes balanced class weights and the survival head takes None, so it touches degradation_regressor_p10/p50/p90 and nothing else. 08q - FOUR OF FIVE on substance: theta_air appears only in int_dirty_air_tax_component.sql (:168-231, and nowhere else under transform/models), so it moves dirty_air_tax_s, which sits inside driver_skill_residual_s and therefore inside DEGRADATION_TARGET and CLIFF_TARGET - while STINT_LIFE_TARGET is synthesised in features.py from stint_length_laps - lap_in_stint and no dirty-air FEATURE column carries theta (dirty_air_thermal_load_* come from int_lap_air_state, which never reads it). THE MECHANICAL FACT THAT MAKES THE BUNDLE REAL, and it is stronger than 'four items each want a retrain': a version is not per-model. S.MODEL_VERSION_DEFAULT (schema.py:361, currently v12) is ONE constant, and train.py, evaluate.py, predict.py, export_onnx.py, card.py and tune.py all default to it; predict.py:43-76 loads all five artefacts at a single version and raises FileNotFoundError on a missing booster. So a v13 exists only once all five .bst files exist at v13, and `make ml-retrain` is train.py --all --tuned, one command over PRODUCTION_TARGETS. Landing any ONE of the four costs the same five fits, the same re-export, the same card/ONNX/predictions rebuild and the same re-quoting; landing them separately pays that four times and re-strands the previous bump's figures each time. The sequencing question is now tracked as D16. D10's own question is unchanged and unanswered.
decisions.recommendation: AUDIT 2026-09-18: DO NOT LAND for the wrap-up. Floor 1 clears on one family of five (p50) and 08i itself records it as a preference, not a gate pass. The cost is larger than the rebuild and retrain: every substrate change strands every published figure - the leaf doc's own live example is that no 10b-10e figure reproduces to six decimals on v12. Bundling with 10e's S1x landing does not make it cheap: S1x retrains one model, while the floor revert retrains all five plus a dbt rebuild. Whatever is decided, correct schema.yml's stint_baseline_pace description (it documents floor 1; the SQL runs floor 2).

decisions.question: Spend 1-2 weeks of fable-5.1 on 03c (AKM two-way FE on degradation slope with the Kline-Saggio-Solvsten leave-out correction), or close it unstarted?
decisions.context: PLAIN VERSION. 03c asks how much of tyre degradation is the driver and how much is the car, using drivers who changed teams to tell the two apart. Its inputs are done: 03a said GO on 2018-2024 alone, and 03b widened the panel to 42 movers in one connected component. Nothing is technically wrong with it. The limited-mobility bias the leaf doc warns about is exactly what the leave-out estimator corrects, and 'how much the correction moved the answer' is the deliverable. The case against is cost and payoff: 1-2 weeks of the most expensive model, no reusable leave-out machinery in the tree (01b built a different estimator and closed failing its own gate), and the leaf doc itself expects wide standard errors because the 'firm' is constructor x season. It feeds nothing on the ML ladder; its value is a publishable finding. An earlier reason given in the 2026-09-18 audit for dropping it - that the bias runs in the direction of the claim - was wrong and is withdrawn.
decisions.recommendation: A cost call, not a technical one. For a short wrap-up: close it unstarted with the GO verdict and this reasoning on record, so a later session can reopen it cold. If driver-vs-car in degradation is a finding you want published, it is the only item left that produces a new one.

decisions.resolution: YES - admit 02b's qualifying columns (arms A, B, C) into FEATURE_COLUMNS for cliff_classifier only. Degrade trio stays at 32 columns (no p90 admission despite B/C clearing individually). Execute as part of v12->v13 bundle with D10, 08o and 08q. Rationale: cliff_classifier cleared decisively on all three arms (4.6x-6.8x floor); degradation trio did not clear sufficiently to warrant the contract change at this time.
decisions.question: Admit 02b's qualifying-derived columns (arms B and/or C) into FEATURE_COLUMNS for cliff_classifier (all three arms clear decisively) and/or degradation_regressor_p90 (B and C clear individually, the 7-column union does not)?
decisions.context: 02b is GATED 2026-09-19: gates 1-6 ran and passed, gate 7 (e-BH) cannot reject under Construction B's n=5,g=1 ceiling (36) against any campaign family of two or more - a permanent, structural non-rejection for all 20 of this item's declared arms (see 09c and 02b's leaf-doc sec.11), not evidence the effect is absent. Floor-clearing (gate 3) and the permutation-null information split (gate 4) are the instruments that carried: cliff clears at roughly 4.6x-6.8x its floor on all three arms (C beats B, so the driver's one-lap form carries the signal, not the car term); p90 clears on B and C individually but the 7-column union (A) fails from dilution - the mirror image of the Phase 10a capacity trap. Landing costs a FEATURE_COLUMNS contract bump (32 -> more), a retrain/re-export of whichever targets are touched (cliff_classifier at minimum, optionally degradation_regressor_p90), and the same version-bump discipline 08n argued for a target/contract change. Separately unresolved and NOT a precondition for this decision: 04c's authoritative campaign-wide e-BH re-run over the 103+ declared hypotheses (09c's finding) - it cannot flip 02b's own gate-7 non-rejection (categorical per 09c's ceiling arithmetic, since E_max(5,1)=36 < 20x2=40) but could in principle surface a joint rejection touching other near-ceiling items; that is 04c's undone job, not this one's. BUNDLING NOTE 2026-09-19, added by the build-order restructure, and NOT a change to this decision's status. See the matching note on D10: D12 and D10 both terminate in a retrain, a re-export and a version bump, so ruling them together costs one bump instead of two, and new item 08o is a third candidate for the same bundle. SEPARATELY, one piece of evidence that does bear on the ANSWER here and was not available when this decision was raised: ml/artefacts/evaluation_metrics.json's `attainable` block (evaluated 2026-09-19, v12, the current substrate) puts degradation_regressor_p90 at fraction_of_attainable_in_sample 0.6796591516491961 while p10 and p50 are already PAST their own bound at 1.2045005970277398 and 1.0771127196576855. That denominator is exact for stint-constant predictors, not an estimate. So p90 is the only degradation head with measurable headroom on the current substrate - and p90 is precisely the head 02b's arms B and C moved. That does not decide D12 and the arms still have to be re-scored post-08m before any delta is quoted; it means the p90 half of this question is aimed at the one degradation head where there is anything left to win. New item 01c writes that block up properly and is now the pointer; worth reading before ruling. RETRAIN-BUNDLE CROSS-REFERENCE 2026-09-20, added by the clubbing pass. Status untouched. The bundle is now four items - 08i (D10), 02b (this one), 08o and 08q - and the matching note on D10 carries each one's traced artefact footprint plus the mechanical reason a version bump is set-wide rather than per-model (S.MODEL_VERSION_DEFAULT is one constant; predict.py:43-76 loads all five artefacts at it). The sequencing call is now D16. ONE FINDING THAT BEARS ON THE SHAPE OF THIS QUESTION'S ANSWER, traced this session and not recorded anywhere before: 'cliff_classifier and/or degradation_regressor_p90' is not fully expressible in the current schema. Per-family masking IS supported - ml/src/features.py:176-179 looks up S.PER_TARGET_FEATURE_MASK by TARGET_BY_NAME[target].family, and a masked family's matrix and fingerprint are unchanged because features.py:206 fingerprints over feature_cols AFTER the mask - so admitting the quali columns globally to FEATURE_COLUMNS and masking them from the families that should not see them is a move the code already makes. But the key is the FAMILY, and schema.py:298-304 gives p10, p50 and p90 the single family 'degradation_regressor'. So 'admit to p90 only' cannot be expressed by masking: it means admitting to all three quantile heads, or a code change keying the mask by target name. That is a fact about the machinery, not an argument either way, and it belongs in front of whoever rules on the p90 half.

decisions.question: May a declared-but-disowned e-value be withdrawn from the campaign's e-BH family before 04c's authoritative union run, or does 09c's non-retroactivity rule bind it in regardless?
decisions.context: Found by the 2026-09-19 build-order audit while checking whether 04c's deferred union e-BH is actually benign. It is not: sorted descending against the e-BH rung 103/(0.05*k), the top five declared E's clear a joint rejection today (k*=5): 10d's A4x depth-2 and A4 depth-3 (Construction A, 1.1e11 and 9.3e8), and 11b's E1/E3/E2 (1996/1010/1000). decisions.question: Should 08i (D10), 02b (D12), 08o and 08q land as ONE v12 -> v13 rebuild, or as separate version bumps as each is ruled?
decisions.context: Raised 2026-09-20 by the clubbing pass, in answer to the user's question 'can we club certain fixes together?'. It is a SEQUENCING call and not a fifth technical question: it does not ask whether any of the four should land. D10 and D12 ask that for two of them, and 08o's and 08q's leaf docs are each required to RECOMMEND 'ride the bundle or go alone' (work/08-foundations-repair.md, 08o definition of done clause 3; 08q clause 4). Those two clauses have had nowhere to land - 08o and 08q are items, not decisions, so their recommendation would arrive as prose with nothing in decisions[] holding it, the same gap D15 was raised to close for publishing. WHY IT IS ONE OPERATION AND NOT FOUR, verified from source this session: S.MODEL_VERSION_DEFAULT (ml/src/schema.py:361) is a single constant, currently v12; train.py, evaluate.py, predict.py, export_onnx.py, card.py and tune.py all default to it; predict.py:43-76 loads all five artefacts at one version and raises FileNotFoundError if any booster is missing at it. A version therefore EXISTS only when all five .bst files exist at it, and `make ml-retrain` (train.py --all --tuned) is one command looping S.PRODUCTION_TARGETS. WHAT EACH MEMBER ACTUALLY MOVES, traced rather than assumed: 08i all five fits (the four thermal columns are in FEATURE_COLUMNS and unmasked); 02b the classifier at minimum, and see D12 on why the family-level mask makes 'p90 only' unexpressible; 08o three of five (train.py::_sample_weight applies survival_weight only to spec.kind == 'quantile'); 08q four of five on substance (theta_air is confined to int_dirty_air_tax_component.sql and moves the label for the trio and the classifier, while STINT_LIFE_TARGET is synthesised in features.py and does not carry it). The UNION is all five either way, and the fifth artefact is re-cut by the version convention whether or not its fit moved. THE COST OF NOT BUNDLING is the one D10's own recommendation already names: 'a second bump re-strands every figure the first one re-published'. Four sequential bumps means four rounds of re-quoting across 08e/08f/08h/02/11a and the model card, and four overwrites of ml/artefacts/evaluation_metrics.json - which is gitignored (.gitignore:77), so each overwrite destroys the previous substrate's figures. That is not hypothetical: it is exactly how 01c's pre-10e oracle became unrecoverable. WHAT THIS DECISION IS NOT. It blocks nothing and no item carries blocked_by_decision D16: 08i already waits on D10 and 02b on D12, and 08o's and 08q's own measurements write nothing to ml/models/ or ml/artefacts/ and can run under any answer. It also does not force simultaneity - 'one bump' means the four rulings are collected and then EXECUTED once, which is compatible with ruling them weeks apart. And it merges nothing: all four keep their own ids and their own definitions of done, because each is independently checkable. A FIFTH CANDIDATE, later and larger, named so it is not missed: 12a's FORWARD direction (ingest 2025) changes the training set and the holdout by itself - ml/src/features.py:54-57 resolves holdout_season as MAX(race_year) + 1 - so it carries the same bump and 12a's own note already prices it as 'a v13 carrying the same re-quoting cost D10 is currently being weighed against'. If that direction is taken it SUBSUMES this bundle rather than joining it, and the four rulings would want to be in hand before it runs.

verified: CRPS reduces EXACTLY to MAE for a point forecast (all three quantiles equal), not just approximately -- the pinball loss is linear in alpha for fixed q (no kink, since y>=q is alpha-independent), so the 3-point trapezoid integrates it exactly regardless of grid spacing; ml/tests/test_crps.py::test_crps_reduces_to_mae_for_a_point_forecast checks this to rel=1e-9.

mcb - dsc + unc reconstructs crps to float precision by pure algebra (unconditional on how `recal` is defined); dsc >= 0 always holds for the binned method because the K-bin per-bin-optimal fit is a strict relaxation of the 1-bin global-constant fit `unc` uses. mcb carries NO such guarantee under binning (only under full isotonic/PAV recalibration, which this is not) -- confirmed against real data, not just theory: the first real run (degradation trio, cv_final_fold, n=13,896, eval_season=2024) landed mcb=-0.0049, dsc=1.2994, unc=2.7647, crps=1.4604 -- a negative mcb happened on the first real try, meaning the trio carries real within-bin information a bin constant cannot capture, not a defect in the arithmetic.

Ran `python -m ml.src.evaluate` on the live degradation trio against data/dev.duckdb (real models, real cv_final_fold split) and confirmed report['crps'] is emitted with the expected shape; then ran the full `make ml-evaluate` (all 4 targets) to leave ml/artefacts/evaluation_metrics.json in its normal complete state rather than the partial one the targeted check produced.

The pre-registered ANOVA cross-check FAILED its declared ~2dp tolerance: ceiling.py::variance_components gives a stint ICC of 0.174836 on the identical rows against REML's 0.199020, gap +0.024183.

Cause traced by simulation on the real stint design at a known ICC of 0.195122: gaussian noise gives a gap of -0.000497, target-shaped (skew -0.81, excess kurtosis 5.02) +0.000312, heteroscedastic -0.001547, but AR(1) at rho=0.60 gives +0.018586. Only serial correlation splits the two estimators, and rho=0.60 is the lag-1 autocorrelation ceiling.py already measures (within_stint_lag1_autocorr 0.6044) from the 5-lap window overlap.

Under that AR(1) both estimators inflate hard: a true ICC of 0.195122 is read as 0.326886 (ANOVA) and 0.345472 (REML), ~70% overstatement of the between-stint share. This is the mechanism behind ceiling.py's existing non_overlapping correction.

METHOD: the reseed floor alone is the wrong denominator for a last-leg gain. It is the sd of the headline under seed-only refits of the SAME rows; the last leg differs in its rows too. The 100% point has no subsample variance, the 75% point is a mean over three draws carrying sd_75/sqrt(3), so the floor is 2*sqrt(sd_75^2/3 + sd_reseed^2). It changes a verdict: stint life's last leg reads as a real gain against the reseed floor (+0.00655 vs 0.00281) and is inside noise against the correct one (0.00887), because stint life has the largest subsample sd of the five. IDENTIFICATION: the pairwise difference d = y1 - y2 is exactly symmetric for every eps, because (eps1,eps2) =d (eps2,eps1) implies d =d -d. Demonstrated numerically as well as derived -- unit.py, 400k rows of clean synthetic cells with arbitrary cell means and a known Johnson SU noise, returns sum-of-centred-cubes = -4.7e-12 at m=2 with denominator exactly 0. So defect 1's proposed fix ('fit a skew-capable family to d and back out eps's quantiles') recovers zero skew by construction and reproduces the p10=p90 collapse it was written to remove.

The same unit test validates the replacement arithmetic: sigma^2 recovered to +/-0.5% at m = 2/3/5/10/20 in the presence of arbitrary cell means; gamma1 to within +/-4.4% at m>=3 and undefined at m=2; gamma2 to within +/-6.4% at every m INCLUDING m=2, so tail weight is identified from pairs while skew is not.

Arm 1 diagnostics on the eval population: L3 covers 13,678 of 13,896 rows (98.4%) in 1,276 cells, median 10 members, max 36; 1,152 cells hold m>=3 (13,430 rows). Of the 30 unmatched feature columns only two carry any NaN (ahead_identity_stability 28.4%, surface_bulk_ratio 10.8%). Admissible-neighbour distance over those 30 columns, standardised: p05 1.466 / median 4.275 / p95 9.187 against 3.477 / 6.829 / 12.166 for random pairs -- a 37% reduction that nowhere approaches zero, so no extrapolation to zero distance was run and defect 5's own stated rule is the reason.

THE PRE-REGISTERED NULL ARM FAILED ON ITS FIRST PASS (-39.7%/-39.5%/-21.9% at L0/L1/L2) AND FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THE RULES AROUND THE ESTIMATOR, not in the estimator. (a) The one-row-per-stint admissibility rule took the lowest lap_in_stint, which wherever the rule binds selects early-stint rows -- and the noise is heteroscedastic in lap_in_stint. Repaired by drawing the row at random over 8 seeds; at L3 the rule binds on nothing and the repair moves L3 by exactly 0.0000. (b) Standardising the shape on circuit x compound x lap_band (259 strata, ~24 rows each) normalises each small group by a scale its own outlier inflated and returned excess kurtosis 37.3% LOW; the unstandardised pooled version returned it 67.5% HIGH on the scale mixture; the coarse compound x lap_band (22 strata) recovers it to +0.5%. After both repairs the null arm passes at every ladder level, worst +4.13%.

Arm 6 re-run at the shape actually claimed (gamma1 -0.5935, gamma2 +5.1086), 5 repetitions on the real X and the real cell structure with skewed heteroscedastic noise: null arm sigma^2 -1.98% +/- 2.14%, end-to-end p50 floor +3.4%. assumed: That the +17.0% mean-function bias the full synthetic arm measures at L3 transfers to the real data in MAGNITUDE. It does not transfer and is not used as one -- only the DIRECTION is used, and the direction is a theorem (Var(y|cell) = Var(f|cell) + E[sigma^2|cell] >= E[sigma^2|cell]) rather than a simulation result. The synthetic f is invented and its within-cell variation was never calibrated against the real residual's.

That conditioning the estimator on the race is acceptable, quantified only through arm 5's ICC on the PRODUCTION MODEL'S residuals. Every 2024 circuit hosts exactly one race, so the different-race half of defect 5's independence constraint was unavailable and was dropped rather than faked; arm 5 prices it at 4.5% using the incumbent's own residuals, which is a model-dependent read on a bias affecting a floor meant to bound that same model.

That the standardised shape (gamma1 -0.5935, gamma2 +5.1086) describes the NOISE rather than the noise plus the mean-function bias's own shape. The full synthetic arm measures the attenuation at x0.601 and x0.514, so the true noise is more skewed and heavier-tailed than reported; de-attenuating by those factors moves the floors by only +1.8% / -4.0% / -3.5%, which is why the shape is treated as a second-order term rather than corrected.

That a Johnson SU is the right two-parameter shape family for this noise. It was chosen because it covers the (skew, kurtosis) region this target sits in and has a tested ppf in scipy, not because anything was fitted against an alternative. No competing family (skew-t, two-piece normal, NIG) was run, so the lambda values carry an unmeasured family-choice component.

That the L4 and L5 rungs are informative about the residual bias at L3 despite being 4- and 5-coordinate matches outside the regime R1's dimension constraint permits, and despite their coverage falling to 0.934 and 0.835. They are read only as a direction (the ladder is still falling), never as floors.

That the p90 result is a conditional-shape finding for 11a rather than a model-family one for 05a. The argument is 01a's -- p90's row arm was the weakest of the trio and its recency signal the only mixed one of the five -- but nothing was run to separate 'the upper tail is mis-shaped' from 'the upper tail needs a different model'.

That the per-stratum aggregate's achieved column (0.4894 / 0.9667 / 0.5348) differing from the published headline (0.5188 / 1.0163 / 0.5600) is population and not disagreement. It is the 1,336 rows in sub-30 strata being harder than average; the two were never differenced, per protocol anchoring.

Pattern: the column itself adds noise; shuffled version is pure noise with no alignment to label. Conclusion: REJECTED on all three targets.

CLIFF CLASSIFIER (macro F1, higher-is-better) shows +0.0024, a GAIN, with permutation-null showing shuffled −0.0008 (worse). Difference 0.0032 suggests genuine information signal present, though small.

STINT-LIFE REGRESSOR (AFT nloglik, lower-is-better) shows −0.0096 nloglik, an IMPROVEMENT (lower is better in AFT context). Permutation-null shows shuffled ≈0.0 (no-op), real −0.0096 (improvement). Pattern: weak but real information signal from count alignment.

PAIR ARM (count + push_residual) produces identical scores to single-column arm. push_residual is already in the baseline (part of 'driver_push' channel), so the redundant pair adds nothing new. Conclusion: the column-alone delta stands, and the design does not answer whether the model wants 'uncertainty' vs 'another counter.'

DECLARABILITY HAZARD IS REAL AND VERIFIED: baseline_observations_n's NULLs are deterministic on count-of-valid-prior-laps (0 at lap 1, 1.0 mean at lap 2, up to 75 overall; mean 12.5), which is NOT a contract axis. The exact missingness pattern depends on stint_length_laps, which is (a) a member of IDENTIFIER_COLUMNS (not for features), (b) strongly correlated with the synthesized target (remaining_stint_life_laps = stint_length_laps − lap_in_stint), and (c) not declared as an axis for missingness. Putting the count in X makes model behavior depend on an undeclared axis, violating the declarability framework.
assumed: Cliff and stint-life's information signals are small enough to be within measurement noise or session-specific seed variation. Neither passes the threshold of 'information exceeds floor' by a margin that would justify overriding the declarability hazard.

The degradation family's losses are attributable to the count itself (model learning a spurious association with the label via the missingness pattern), not to model capacity. The permutation-null supports this -- the shuffled version is worse than real in all three targets, indicating the real column is not purely additive noise but rather a learned spurious relationship.

The pair arm's redundancy (push_residual already in baseline) is a design flaw rather than a substantive finding about the column. A true test of 'uncertainty vs counter' would require push_residual to not already be present, which is not this experiment's condition.

The floor (all targets showed noise floor = 0.0 due to tree-based model determinism on fixed eval data) is not a limiting factor in this gate; the arm deltas and permutation-null are the measurements.

baseline_observations_n will remain useful for external consumers and audit (visible to future modelers, allowing them to condition on the count if they rebuild), so shipping it in the mart without putting it in FEATURE_COLUMNS is the right compromise.

history.landed: 10c re-measured on repaired metrics and its record corrected. Four defects found in the 10c metric code (all of it written in the same uncommitted batch that produced the original result, all of it untested): (1) d_calibration was a TAUTOLOGY - it evaluated each row's survival curve at that row's own predicted median, so z==0 and predicted risk was exactly 0.5 for every row; all 5 bins collapsed and the slope returned null. The observed side mirrored it, using KM at each bin's own median. Both now use a shared horizon. (2) ipcw_brier was not IPCW - both branches of its censored/uncensored conditional were byte-identical and weights ignored the horizon, scoring rows censored before t as though they had failed by t; now Graf et al. weighting. (3) time_dependent_auc counted ties as discordant and let y==t sit in both risk sets; ties now take half credit, at-risk is strictly y>t, and the O(n^2) loop is vectorised. (4) dependence_strength 1.2x WITHDRAWN - cause determines censoring status under 10b so those rates are 0/1 by construction, and the band tau in [0, min(0.5,.)] returns [0,0.5] for any input. Eight regression tests added in ml/tests/test_survival.py (26 pass); these three functions had zero coverage before, which is how a tautology survived a full measurement run.
verified: 10c honest headline: green_pit (tyre-limit) IPCW-Brier 0.141, time-dependent AUC 0.844, calibration slope 1.232. Artefact ml/artefacts/10c_evaluation_results.json.

The 'overall' row (Brier 0.093, AUC 0.924) is the 10b mixture artefact in a new metric and is now labelled diagnostic_only_conflates_causes in the artefact. Under 10b censoring green_pit is the ONLY uncensored cause, so 'overall' scores green-pit events against an at-risk pool 54% non-green whose lengths differ by construction (race_end 26.4 laps mean, green_pit 20.4, red 5.3). Superseded figures: green-pit AUC 0.829, overall Brier 0.116, overall AUC 0.916, and an unsupported 'calibration slope ~1 (unbiased)'.

CALIBRATION DEFECT (the finding): stint_life_regressor over-predicts stint life, worst where it matters. Green-pit observed risk exceeds predicted in 4 of 5 bins and the gap widens with risk - top bin predicted 0.78 against observed 0.95.

The defect is the MODEL'S, not an SC-selection artefact. Races with zero SC/VSC stint endings had no diversion, so green_pit there is an unfiltered sample of the tyre limit. Slope is flat across that split: 1.224 (zero-SC, n=6822) vs 1.267 (SC races, n=2448) vs 1.232 (all), with AUC identical to three decimals. Cluster bootstrap over races on the zero-SC stratum, 200 draws: mean 1.222, sd 0.0714, 95% interval [1.0984, 1.3626], 0 of 200 draws below 1.0.

Repaired d_calibration validated against data drawn from the lognormal AFT it assumes: returns slope 1.03 at 0% censoring, 0.98 at 20%, 0.93 at 40%. green_pit has no censoring within it (the 1.03 case), so 1.23 is the model's miscalibration and not the metric's bias.

New finding, mine: a lap spanning a status change carries every code in effect, so a pitting car's longer lap is mechanically likelier to pick up the '4'. Across the 276 non-unanimous slices, pit laps are flagged 85.63% vs 42.95% for non-pit (n=508 / 2,084), and these carry 435 of the 1,440 treated pit moments (30.2%). Bounded, not fatal: dropping all 1,330 mixed-slice Z=1 moments leaves L5a at RR 6.950 / 1,337 pairs (L3 4.408 -> 3.789), still 3.5x the pre-registered floor. Retention on that subset is 1,382/5,637 = 24.5%, below the 30% bar, and is recorded in the leaf doc as such.

Ladder B is MORE exposed to that channel, not less: 31.8% of onset moments and 36.0% of onset pit moments sit on mixed slices against 19.1% of all Z=1, so its stronger RR is partly artefact. Recorded so 07b does not mistake the onset restriction for the conservative one.

history.landed: MEASUREMENT AND A WRITTEN DECISION; nothing shipped, no contract or warehouse change. Wrote the full 06b pre-registration into work/06-publication.md (estimand, population, deviation, four-rung estimator ladder, clustering, the pre-declared era contrast, three named falsifications, corner classes and thresholds, the mechanism prediction) BEFORE any coefficient was fitted, then ran it: scratchpad/d0-d3 (throwaway, not committed), panel_06b_lap.parquet and panel_06b_corner.parquet (cached, not committed), 06b_dirty_air_per_season.json (93 fits) and 06b_diagnostics.json. The item's framing changed at gate 1: the shipped theta_air = 0.5 is not an estimate at all. int_lap_air_state.dirty_air_share_lap is BINARY (127,310 zeros / 35,419 ones, a MAX over the single S2 sector), int_dirty_air_tax_component's calibration_panel filters it to > 0, and a constant regressor gives VAR_POP = 0, so NULLIF returns NULL and the SQL's own COALESCE(..., 0.5) supplies the number. The warehouse has been charging following cars a flat 0.5 s/lap since 2018 on a fallback prior. Refit per season with both arms kept: +0.396 / +0.151 / +0.170 / +0.083 / +0.011 / +0.045 / -0.036 s/lap (2018-2024, F2 = stint FE + tyre-age bins, race-clustered 95% CI); 0.5 lies outside the interval in six of seven seasons. The pre-declared 2022 contrast came back correctly signed and strongly significant (Delta = -0.219 [-0.331, -0.106], p = 0.0002) and the post-hoc falsifications killed it as a regulation story: placebo era boundaries fire at every season from 2019 to 2024 with 2022 the second-weakest, a linear season trend fits at -0.0667/season (p < 0.0001), and dropping 2018 alone shrinks Delta to -0.163. Corner-type breakdown on the apex-speed deficit with driver x race x corner FE: fast-corner deficit falls 0.63% -> 0.39% of apex speed and slow corners do not move at all -- the exact ordering the pre-declared downforce mechanism predicts, with not one of the three Deltas distinguishable from zero. The precise corner result is the level rather than the change: the cornering deficit is flat across all seven seasons while the lap-level cost collapsed. Decided IN WRITING to keep the global theta in production, because dirty_air_tax_s is subtracted inside driver_skill_residual_s and fct_cliff_prediction_features builds its regression target as a lead-difference of that column -- the tax is inside the label, so changing it is a gated change that rewrites the target for every model in the programme. The full-sequence lag is load-bearing and was checked. Computing the lag AFTER the model's filters instead of before gives a 2018 treatment mean of 0.1796 against the shipped 0.1969; the panel builder therefore lags over int_stint_geometry's complete stint sequence and filters afterwards, which is what the model's full_sequence_lag CTE does.

The label-lineage argument was traced in the SQL, not assumed: fct_cliff_prediction_features lines 490-573 build next_lap_degradation_jump_s and its detrended sibling as LEAD-differences of driver_skill_residual_s, int_lap_residual_decomposed line 241 subtracts COALESCE(dirty_air_tax_s, 0.0) when forming it, and ml/src/schema.py lists driver_skill_residual_s in EXCLUDED_LEAKAGE_COLUMNS as 'literally encode the label'.

The defect's footprint on the label is measured, not estimated: the following state flips between t-1 and t on 14.33% of panel laps (12.59% in 2018 rising to 15.69% in 2022), and the training label's own sd is 0.9884 s with a median absolute value of 0.3625 s over the 114,507 is_training_eligible rows.

The deviation-2 contamination channel was measured and dismissed rather than argued away: following moves the driver's own S2 trap speed by between -0.209 and +0.242 km/h, and every season's 95% CI spans zero, so the dt_per_dm rescaling of braking_loss_s and exit_residual_s is not material.

Every result is reported at four estimator rungs (no FE / driver x race FE / stint + tyre-age FE / the same minus laps within two of an SC, VSC, red-flag or pit lap) and all four agree on the shape: large in 2018, indistinguishable from zero by 2022.

The three headline coefficients were recomputed from scratch and match pyfixest exactly: a hand-written alternating-projection demeaning over stint_id and age_bin followed by plain OLS returns +0.3955941954 (2018), +0.0107991272 (2022) and -0.0360629124 (2024) against pyfixest's absorbed fit, max difference 1.6e-13 -- ruling out a demeaning-shortcut bug in the FE absorption. d1_build_panels_06b.py was also re-run end to end and returns the identical 123,993 / 780,160 row counts and the same 1e-9 reproduction.

The alternative -- that a real 2022 step sits on top of a pre-existing trend -- is not excluded by anything run here, and the data has nowhere near the power to separate them.

The corner-class mechanism claim is DIRECTIONAL ONLY. The fast-corner point estimate falls and the slow-corner one does not, which is what a wake-sensitivity change predicts, but all three era Deltas straddle zero and fast corners are only ~15% of corner rows. Nothing here confirms the aero channel.

history.session: 06c run: corner-phase skill publication with Verstappen anomaly
history.landed: POST DRAFTED. mart_corner_skill_driver (139 populated driver-seasons, 2018-2024) extracted and verified row-by-row from the Sep 13 parquet rebuild. Phase decomposition: braking, mid-corner, exit residuals per (driver, race, corner, season) with LORO same-car baseline. Norris 2024 leads at index -3.17, 69% exit contribution (-0.267s from 76 cells against -0.042s braking from 305 cells). Full 2024 field (20 drivers) tabled with all three SEs and cell counts. The index is a sum of three within-season z-scores over winsorized (driver, race, corner) cells with PHASE_MIN_CELLS=30 floor; only 139 driver-seasons clear it. Discovered and explained the zero-sum property in two-car teams: because the LORO baseline in a two-driver team is just the other driver, 57 of 69 team-seasons are exact sign mirrors with mean absolute team-season sum = 0.048. The index cannot see team-wide strength, and drivers with weak/strong teammates are not on the same scale. Cross-team comparison not supported. VER anomaly: braking +0.0745s (weak, second-worst in field), mid-corner -0.0745s (strong, best-in-field). Contradicts received wisdom about his late/trail braking. Shown to persist across six of seven seasons (2018-2024) against four different teammates (RIC, GAS, ALB, PER 3x). Two candidate explanations named: (a) real trail-braking style trading entry time for apex speed, (b) braking sign is backwards. Post argues both through independent evidence and correlation structure: 06b found that dirty air (unambiguously bad) produces negative braking_loss_s in every corner class and era; braking and mid-corner correlate -0.52 across all 139 driver-seasons (would expect positive if both measured skill). Why not flip the sign: flipping it doesn't fix the index, relocates the problem (VER 7th->2nd but Gasly 17th->1st). Deeper issue: all three phases mutually negatively correlated (braking-mid -0.52, mid-exit -0.22, braking-exit -0.16), product of three negatives is negative, so no sign assignment makes all three pairwise-positive. Three phases together vary 21% less than under independence (sd 0.092s vs 0.117s), suggesting genuine corner trade-off. External check named to settle the question: corners with known braking points from independent source; confirm whether later braking predicts faster or slower corner, car fixed. Draft post in scratchpad, 256 lines including full methodology, caveats, and two-phase results section.
verified: All 20 driver rows × 10 fields (three phases + index + SEs + cell counts) verified row-by-row against the current parquet (mart_corner_skill_driver, rebuilt Sep 13). Norris 2024 index -3.17, exit -0.2669s, braking -0.0424s. VER 2024 braking +0.0745s, mid-corner -0.0745s. All arithmetic (sign mirrors, correlations, cell-count distributions) checked.
Population count: 139 driver-seasons verified in the data. Two driver-seasons (2019 Norris and Sainz) excluded as expected on the 21 exit-cell floor at PHASE_MIN_CELLS=30.

Zero-sum property confirmed: 57 of 69 two-driver team-seasons carry exact sign-mirror pairs (VER/PER, NOR/PIA, HAM/RUS, ALO/STR, ZHO/BOT, SAI/LEC, GAS/OCO all sign-flipped). Mean absolute index sum within team-season = 0.048 (effectively zero).
Mirror-pair arithmetic: Norris -3.17 / -0.267 exit / Piastri +3.17 / +0.267 exit; VER -0.37 / +0.0745 braking / PER +0.37 / -0.0745 braking; all exact sign negatives.

Correlation structure: braking-mid -0.52, mid-exit -0.22, braking-exit -0.16 (all 139 driver-seasons). Variance decomposition: three phases together sd 0.092s vs 0.117s under independence (21% variance reduction).

VER pattern persistence: six of seven seasons show positive (weak) braking: 2018 RIC baseline -0.004s, 2019 GAS +0.049s, 2020 ALB +0.157s, 2021 PER +0.077s, 2022 PER +0.043s, 2023 PER +0.040s, 2024 PER +0.075s. Mid-corner negative (strong) in all seven. Different teammate in each period rules out teammate-specific artefact.
assumed: The two candidate explanations (real trail-braking style vs. braking sign bug) are genuinely unresolved by the data. Both have supporting evidence: the correlation structure and independent physics-anchored signal from 06b support the sign-bug hypothesis; the observed trading of entry time for apex speed is coherent under the real-style hypothesis. No internal measurement resolves it.

The zero-sum property is a constraint of the LORO same-car baseline design, not a defect. It is a feature that differences out the car; the trade-off is that team-wide strength is invisible and cross-team comparison is not supported. The post names this plainly.

Exit is the thinnest phase (median 199 cells vs 284 mid-corner, 257 braking) and carries the largest spread across drivers (sd 0.097s vs 0.056s braking, 0.035s mid). Norris's 76 exit cells are joint-lowest in 2024. The headline (exit is 69% of his index) rests on this thin phase. Reported honestly: 6.8 standard errors from zero so not noise, but precision is overstated.
All 139 driver-seasons populated. 141 total clear the 100-mapped-corner admission floor; 2019 Norris and Sainz excluded on 21 exit cells. Rookie and part-seasons largely absent.

The standard errors are within-phase only (sd / sqrt(N) per phase), do not propagate into the index, assume cell independence when laps within a race are not independent, and take LORO baseline as known. Treat as precision floor, not confidence interval.
No brake-pressure traces, steering, IMU. Braking point is first sample with brake flag set at the public feed sampling rate. Teams with real data would measure better, particularly on braking.

assumed: That delta(1) = 0 for both tyres -- i.e. that a freshly fitted set starts at the same unmodelled-pace level the outgoing set started at. The level multiplies L + (H-L) = H and cancels from the argmin ONLY if it is the same for both tyres; if it is not, the argmin moves. Not testable from the substrate, because the new tyre's age-1 pace under the counterfactual stop lap was never observed.

That the model's local per-lap degradation slope is J(t)/15 + drift, from J(t) = sum_{j=1..5}(rho(t+j) - rho(t)) - 15*drift under local linearity of rho over the 5-lap window. The deconvolution is exact only if rho is linear inside the window.

That the induced-policy metric measures decision quality. It does not, quite: the model's delta path is a sequence of 5-lap-ahead forecasts made on the REALISED feature rows, because a DP standing at lap 1 has no feature row for lap 20. What is measured is forecast quality re-expressed in seconds, conditional on the realised path -- not a rollout under a simulator. Stated rather than fixed; fixing it needs a counterfactual feature generator, which is research.

That the 'model' arm's per-stint drift_s_per_lap is contamination rather than information. It is an OLS slope fitted on the stint's own realised residuals, so the arm that uses it (7.46 s) is optimistic; the drift-free arms (9.63 in-sample, 9.32 out of sample) are the honest ones and carry the headline. The size of the contamination -- about 2.2 s/stint -- is measured but its exact provenance is not decomposed.

That the 'known-good' screen (green stint ending AND a points finish) identifies competent strategy calls. It is deliberately non-circular -- it uses no quantity derived from the cost surface -- but it is a proxy: a points finish is a car property as much as a strategy property.
That races are independent, which E1 and E3's betting construction needs. Races within a season share a regulation and a car regime. E2's permutation does not need it.

That the 3.59 s/stint the ML forecast buys would survive being wired into int_pit_strategy_cost_curve itself. It is measured as a post-hoc delta layered on the published cost columns, not as a rebuilt dbt model, and the rebuild would change the target definition's own lineage.

That a hazard with a lap axis would rescue the stochastic arm. Cautions cluster at starts, restarts and late race, and a flat per-lap rate cannot express that -- but nothing here tested a lap-varying hazard, because the table does not hold one.
